source.text: וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן וּלְאַבְשָׁל֧וֹם בֶּן־דָּוִ֛ד אָח֥וֹת יָפָ֖ה וּשְׁמָ֣הּ תָּמָ֑ר וַיֶּאֱהָבֶ֖הָ אַמְנ֥וֹן בֶּן־דָּוִֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after this, and to Absalom son of David [was] a sister beautiful, and her name [was] Tamar; and loved her Amnon son of David.

en.L: And it happened after this: Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister, and her name [was] Tamar, and Amnon the son of David loved her.
en.B: Some time after this, Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and Amnon son of David fell in love with her.
en.R: Later on, David's son Absalom had a beautiful sister named Tamar. Another of David's sons, Amnon, fell in love with her.

es.L: Y sucedió después de esto: Absalón hijo de David tenía una hermana hermosa, y su nombre [era] Tamar, y Amnón hijo de David la amó.
es.B: Algún tiempo después, Absalón hijo de David tenía una hermana hermosa llamada Tamar, y Amnón hijo de David se enamoró de ella.
es.R: Más adelante, Absalón, el hijo de David, tenía una hermana muy hermosa que se llamaba Tamar. Otro de los hijos de David, Amnón, se enamoró de ella.

fr.L: Et il arriva après cela : Absalom, fils de David, avait une sœur belle, et son nom [était] Tamar ; et Amnon, fils de David, l’aima.
fr.B: Quelque temps après, Absalom, fils de David, avait une sœur très belle nommée Tamar, et Amnon, fils de David, s’éprit d’elle.
fr.R: Plus tard, Absalom, le fils de David, avait une très belle sœur qui s’appelait Tamar. Un autre fils de David, Amnon, est tombé amoureux d’elle.

vi.L: Sau việc này, xảy ra như vầy: Áp-sa-lôm con trai Đa-vít có một em gái xinh đẹp, tên [là] Ta-ma, và Am-nôn con trai Đa-vít yêu nàng.
vi.B: Ít lâu sau, Áp-sa-lôm con trai Đa-vít có một em gái xinh đẹp tên là Ta-ma, và Am-nôn, cũng là con trai Đa-vít, đem lòng yêu nàng.
vi.R: Sau đó, Áp-sa-lôm con trai vua Đa-vít có một người em gái rất đẹp tên là Ta-ma. Một người con trai khác của Đa-vít là Am-nôn đem lòng yêu Ta-ma.

decisions.choice: Absalom and Tamar: full brother and sister; Amnon: their half-brother
decisions.reason: Absalom was David's son by Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur (3:3), and Tamar was his full sister. Amnon was David's firstborn, the son of Ahinoam (3:2), so he was Tamar's half-brother and the heir to the throne. Calling both young men "son of David" sets them side by side as rivals within one house.

decisions.choice: loved her: desired her
decisions.reason: The verb covers every kind of love and attraction. What follows shows that Amnon's "love" was desire for her, which turns into hatred once he has had his way (verse 15).

decisions.choice: after this: the trouble foretold to David begins
decisions.reason: The phrase loosely links this story to what came before. Nathan had told David that the sword would never leave his house and that trouble would rise against him from within it (12:10-11). Chapters 13-18 tell how that came about through David's own sons.

decisions.choice: Another of David's sons
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Amnon is a second son of David, not Tamar's full brother; the Hebrew does this by repeating "son of David".

decisions.choice: passé simple for narration at L and B, passé composé at R
decisions.reason: As the French style guide (section 3) and the Samuel terms note set out, for this block of chapters (2 Samuel 13-24): the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative, used at Literal and Balanced; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read today. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

decisions.choice: "s’éprit d’elle" (B); "est tombé amoureux d’elle" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say Amnon became infatuated, as the English "fell in love"; the meaning decision (m2) shows the "love" was desire, which the story itself makes plain in verse 15. Literal keeps "aimer".

decisions.choice: Absalón, Amnón, Tamar; Jonadab, Simea, Talmai, Amiud, Gesur
decisions.reason: For this block of chapters: the names of David's household take their usual Spanish forms, Absalón, Amnón and Tamar, as the terms note has them; the other names of chapter 13 follow the usual Spanish spelling and stay the same through the book.

decisions.choice: "em gái" for Tamar, Absalom's sister
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say whether a sister is older or younger; nothing in the Hebrew says, and Absalom treats her as the one he protects (verse 20), so she is "em gái" to him. Amnon, the firstborn, calls her "em" and himself "anh"; Tamar calls him "anh".

source.text: וַיֵּ֨צֶר לְאַמְנ֜וֹן לְהִתְחַלּ֗וֹת בַּֽעֲבוּר֙ תָּמָ֣ר אֲחֹת֔וֹ כִּ֥י בְתוּלָ֖ה הִ֑יא וַיִּפָּלֵא֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אַמְנ֔וֹן לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָ֖הּ מְאֽוּמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was distress to Amnon to the point of making himself sick because of Tamar his sister, for a virgin [was] she, and it was too difficult in [the] eyes of Amnon to do to her anything.

en.L: And Amnon was so distressed that he made himself sick because of Tamar his sister, for she [was] a virgin, and it was too difficult in the eyes of Amnon to do anything to her.
en.B: Amnon was so tormented over his sister Tamar that he made himself ill. She was a virgin, and it seemed impossible to Amnon to do anything to her.
en.R: Amnon wanted Tamar so badly that he made himself sick over her. She was a virgin, and Amnon thought there was no way he could do anything with her.

es.L: Y Amnón estaba tan angustiado que se enfermó a causa de Tamar su hermana, porque ella [era] virgen, y era demasiado difícil a los ojos de Amnón hacerle algo.
es.B: Amnón estaba tan atormentado por su hermana Tamar que llegó a enfermarse. Ella era virgen, y a Amnón le parecía imposible hacerle nada.
es.R: Amnón deseaba tanto a Tamar que se enfermó por ella. Tamar era virgen, y Amnón pensaba que no había manera de hacer nada con ella.

fr.L: Et Amnon fut tourmenté au point de se rendre malade à cause de Tamar sa sœur, car elle [était] vierge, et il était trop difficile aux yeux d’Amnon de lui faire quoi que ce soit.
fr.B: Amnon était si tourmenté à cause de sa sœur Tamar qu’il en tomba malade. Elle était vierge, et il paraissait impossible à Amnon de rien tenter avec elle.
fr.R: Amnon désirait tellement Tamar qu’il en est tombé malade. Elle était vierge, et Amnon pensait qu’il n’avait aucun moyen d’arriver à ses fins avec elle.

vi.L: Am-nôn bị dày vò đến nỗi tự làm mình đau ốm vì Ta-ma em gái mình, vì nàng [là] một trinh nữ, và trong mắt Am-nôn thật quá khó để làm điều gì với nàng.
vi.B: Am-nôn khổ sở vì Ta-ma em gái mình đến nỗi sinh bệnh. Nàng còn là trinh nữ, và Am-nôn thấy không có cách nào làm gì được nàng.
vi.R: Am-nôn muốn có Ta-ma đến nỗi phát bệnh. Nàng vẫn còn là trinh nữ, và Am-nôn nghĩ rằng mình không thể nào làm gì với nàng được.

decisions.choice: made himself sick: he became ill from his obsession
decisions.reason: The verb form can mean to make oneself sick or to pretend to be sick, as it does in verses 5 and 6. Here it describes how Amnon's frustrated desire wore him down until he was ill; verse 4 shows that it could be seen in his face. Some take it to mean he was already acting sick, but the pretending is Jonadab's idea in verse 5.

decisions.choice: she was a virgin: an unmarried daughter of the king, closely guarded
decisions.reason: A king's unmarried daughters lived in their own quarters and wore a robe that marked them out (verse 18). Amnon could not see her alone without arousing suspicion. The words also show what he wanted: not to marry her but to have her.

decisions.choice: too difficult in his eyes: it seemed impossible to him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of what is beyond someone's power (Genesis 18:14; Deuteronomy 30:11). "In his eyes" means in his own judgment.

decisions.choice: tormented (Balanced); wanted Tamar so badly (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says it was "distress" or "tightness" for Amnon. Balanced says "tormented"; Readable says plainly what the distress was about.

source.text: וּלְאַמְנ֣וֹן רֵ֗עַ וּשְׁמוֹ֙ יֽוֹנָדָ֔ב בֶּן־שִׁמְעָ֖ה אֲחִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וְי֣וֹנָדָ֔ב אִ֥ישׁ חָכָ֖ם מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Amnon [was] a friend, and his name [was] Jonadab son of Shimeah, brother of David; and Jonadab [was] a man shrewd very.

en.L: And Amnon had a friend, and his name [was] Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David's brother. And Jonadab [was] a very shrewd man.
en.B: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother. Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
en.R: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab. He was the son of Shimeah, David's brother, so he was Amnon's cousin. Jonadab was a very clever and crafty man.

es.L: Y Amnón tenía un amigo, y su nombre [era] Jonadab hijo de Simea, hermano de David. Y Jonadab [era] un hombre muy astuto.
es.B: Amnón tenía un amigo llamado Jonadab, hijo de Simea, hermano de David. Jonadab era un hombre muy astuto.
es.R: Amnón tenía un amigo llamado Jonadab. Era hijo de Simea, el hermano de David, así que era primo de Amnón. Jonadab era un hombre muy listo y muy taimado.

fr.L: Et Amnon avait un ami, et son nom [était] Jonadab, fils de Shiméa, frère de David ; et Jonadab [était] un homme très habile.
fr.B: Or Amnon avait un ami nommé Jonadab, fils de Shiméa, le frère de David. Jonadab était un homme très rusé.
fr.R: Amnon avait un ami qui s’appelait Jonadab. C’était le fils de Shiméa, le frère de David ; il était donc le cousin d’Amnon. Jonadab était un homme très malin et très rusé.

vi.L: Am-nôn có một người bạn, tên [là] Giô-na-đáp con trai Si-mê-a, anh của Đa-vít. Giô-na-đáp [là] một người rất khôn lanh.
vi.B: Am-nôn có một người bạn tên là Giô-na-đáp, con trai Si-mê-a, anh của Đa-vít. Giô-na-đáp là người rất khôn lanh.
vi.R: Am-nôn có một người bạn tên là Giô-na-đáp. Anh ta là con trai Si-mê-a, anh của Đa-vít, nên là anh em họ với Am-nôn. Giô-na-đáp là người rất khôn khéo và mưu mẹo.

decisions.choice: shrewd: clever in practical matters, here in a crafty way
decisions.reason: The word usually translated "wise" covers skill of every kind, good or bad. Jonadab's wisdom is cleverness in getting things done; he uses it to plan a crime. The same word describes the woman Joab sends to trick David (14:2).

decisions.choice: Shimeah, David's brother: Jonadab was Amnon's cousin
decisions.reason: Shimeah is the brother called Shammah and Shimea elsewhere, the third son of Jesse (1 Samuel 16:9; 17:13; 1 Chronicles 2:13). His son Jonathan killed a giant at Gath (21:21).

decisions.choice: a friend: a close companion
decisions.reason: The word means a friend or companion. At David's court "the king's friend" was also a title for a trusted adviser (15:37; 16:16), and it may hint that Jonadab was Amnon's confidant at court.

decisions.choice: so he was Amnon's cousin; clever and crafty
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the family tie and uses two words for the one Hebrew word, so that young readers do not take "wise" as praise here.

decisions.choice: Shiméa
decisions.reason: The usual French transcription of the name, with the accent French writes; used for both books.

decisions.choice: muy listo y muy taimado
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, two words for the one Hebrew word (m1), so that the reader does not take 'sabio' as praise: Jonadab's skill is used to plan a crime.

decisions.choice: "khôn lanh" (L, B); "khôn khéo và mưu mẹo" (R)
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "wise" here means cleverness used craftily (meaning decision); "khôn ngoan" would praise him, while "khôn lanh" is quick, practical cleverness. Jonadab and Amnon, cousins of about the same age, speak as "anh" and "tôi".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ מַדּ֣וּעַ אַ֠תָּה כָּ֣כָה דַּ֤ל בֶּן־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בַּבֹּ֣קֶר בַּבֹּ֔קֶר הֲל֖וֹא תַּגִּ֣יד לִ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אַמְנ֔וֹן אֶת־תָּמָ֗ר אֲח֛וֹת אַבְשָׁלֹ֥ם אָחִ֖י אֲנִ֥י אֹהֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, why [are] you thus weak, son of the king, in the morning, in the morning? Will you not tell me? And said to him Amnon, Tamar [the] sister of Absalom my brother I [am] loving.

en.L: And he said to him, "Why [are] you so haggard, son of the king, morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother, I love."
en.B: He asked him, "Why do you look so worn out, son of the king, morning after morning? Will you not tell me?" Amnon answered him, "I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister."
en.R: Jonadab asked him, "You are the king's son! Why do you look so thin and miserable every morning? Tell me what is wrong." Amnon answered, "I am in love with Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."

es.L: Y le dijo: «¿Por qué [estás] tan demacrado, hijo del rey, mañana tras mañana? ¿No me lo dirás?». Y Amnón le dijo: «A Tamar, la hermana de Absalón mi hermano, yo amo».
es.B: Jonadab le preguntó: «¿Por qué te ves tan consumido, hijo del rey, mañana tras mañana? ¿No me lo vas a contar?». Amnón le respondió: «Estoy enamorado de Tamar, la hermana de mi hermano Absalón».
es.R: Jonadab le preguntó: «¡Tú eres el hijo del rey! ¿Por qué te ves tan flaco y tan triste cada mañana? Dime qué te pasa». Amnón le contestó: «Estoy enamorado de Tamar, la hermana de mi hermano Absalón».

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « Pourquoi [es]-tu si défait, fils du roi, matin après matin ? Ne me le diras-tu pas ? » Et Amnon lui dit : « Tamar, la sœur d’Absalom mon frère, je l’aime. »
fr.B: Il lui demanda : « Pourquoi as-tu si mauvaise mine, fils du roi, jour après jour ? Ne veux-tu pas me le dire ? » Amnon lui répondit : « Je suis amoureux de Tamar, la sœur de mon frère Absalom. »
fr.R: Jonadab lui a demandé : « Tu es le fils du roi ! Pourquoi as-tu l’air si maigre et si malheureux chaque matin ? Dis-moi ce qui ne va pas. » Amnon a répondu : « Je suis amoureux de Tamar, la sœur de mon frère Absalom. »

vi.L: Người nói với chàng: "Sao [anh] tiều tụy thế, hỡi con trai của vua, sáng nào cũng vậy? Anh không nói cho tôi biết sao?" Am-nôn nói với người: "Ta-ma, em gái của Áp-sa-lôm em tôi, tôi yêu nàng."
vi.B: Giô-na-đáp hỏi chàng: "Hoàng tử ơi, sao sáng nào trông anh cũng tiều tụy như vậy? Anh không nói cho tôi biết sao?" Am-nôn đáp: "Tôi yêu Ta-ma, em gái của Áp-sa-lôm em tôi."
vi.R: Giô-na-đáp hỏi: "Anh là con của vua mà! Sao sáng nào trông anh cũng gầy gò, khổ sở như thế? Hãy nói cho tôi biết có chuyện gì." Am-nôn trả lời: "Tôi yêu Ta-ma, em gái của Áp-sa-lôm em tôi."

decisions.choice: haggard: thin and worn down
decisions.reason: The word means poor, thin or weak. It is used of Pharaoh's thin cows (Genesis 41:19). Amnon's longing shows in his body.

decisions.choice: in the morning, in the morning: day after day
decisions.reason: Repeating a word in this way means "every" (Exodus 16:21). Jonadab sees him every morning looking worse.

decisions.choice: Tamar, the sister of Absalom my brother: Amnon names her by Absalom
decisions.reason: Amnon puts Tamar first, and calls her Absalom's sister rather than his own. He keeps her at a distance from himself as he speaks, and Absalom's name already stands in the story as the brother who will act for her.

decisions.choice: I am in love with Tamar
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Tamar's name first, as the Hebrew does. Balanced and Readable use ordinary English order. Readable turns the opening question into an exclamation and the second question into a request.

decisions.choice: "Tamar, la sœur d’Absalom mon frère, je l’aime"
alternatives: "J’aime Tamar, la sœur d’Absalom mon frère"
decisions.reason: French can front the object and take it up with a pronoun, as the Hebrew puts Tamar first (m3); Balanced and Readable use the ordinary order.

decisions.choice: A Tamar, la hermana de Absalón mi hermano, yo amo
decisions.reason: Literal keeps Tamar's name first, as the Hebrew and the English Literal do; Spanish marks her as the object with 'a'. Balanced and Readable use the ordinary order 'Estoy enamorado de Tamar'.

decisions.choice: "Áp-sa-lôm em tôi" for "Absalom my brother"
decisions.reason: Amnon was David's firstborn (3:2), Absalom the third son (3:3), so Amnon calls him "em".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יְה֣וֹנָדָ֔ב שְׁכַ֥ב עַל־מִשְׁכָּבְךָ֖ וְהִתְחָ֑ל וּבָ֧א אָבִ֣יךָ לִרְאוֹתֶ֗ךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֡יו תָּ֣בֹא נָא֩ תָמָ֨ר אֲחוֹתִ֜י וְתַבְרֵ֣נִי לֶ֗חֶם וְעָשְׂתָ֤ה לְעֵינַי֙ אֶת־הַבִּרְיָ֔ה לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶרְאֶ֔ה וְאָכַלְתִּ֖י מִיָּדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Jonadab, lie on your bed and make yourself sick, and [when] comes your father to see you, and you will say to him, let come please Tamar my sister and let her give me to eat food, and let her make before my eyes the food, so that I may see, and I will eat from her hand.

en.L: And Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. And when your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please let Tamar my sister come and give me food to eat, and let her prepare the food in my sight, so that I may see [it] and eat from her hand.'"
en.B: Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill. Then, when your father comes to visit you, tell him, 'I beg you, let my sister Tamar come and feed me. Have her prepare the food here in front of me, so that I can watch and then eat it from her hand.'"
en.R: Jonadab told him, "Go to bed and act as if you are sick. Your father will come to see how you are. Ask him, 'Would you let my sister Tamar come and bring me something to eat? I want her to make the food here where I can watch her. Then I will eat it from her hand.'"

es.L: Y Jonadab le dijo: «Acuéstate en tu cama y finge estar enfermo. Y cuando tu padre venga a verte, dile: “Te ruego que venga Tamar mi hermana y me dé de comer, y que prepare la comida ante mis ojos, para que yo [lo] vea y coma de su mano”».
es.B: Jonadab le dijo: «Acuéstate en tu cama y finge que estás enfermo. Luego, cuando tu padre venga a visitarte, dile: “Te suplico que dejes venir a mi hermana Tamar para que me dé de comer. Que prepare la comida aquí delante de mí, para que yo la vea y luego la coma de su mano”».
es.R: Jonadab le aconsejó: «Métete en la cama y haz como si estuvieras enfermo. Tu padre vendrá a ver cómo estás. Pídele: “¿Podrías dejar que mi hermana Tamar venga a traerme algo de comer? Quiero que prepare la comida aquí, donde yo pueda verla. Luego la comeré de su mano”».

fr.L: Et Jonadab lui dit : « Couche-toi sur ton lit et fais le malade. Et quand ton père viendra te voir, tu lui diras : “Que Tamar ma sœur vienne, je te prie, et qu’elle me donne à manger de la nourriture, et qu’elle prépare la nourriture sous mes yeux, afin que je [la] voie et que je mange de sa main.” »
fr.B: Jonadab lui dit : « Mets-toi au lit et fais semblant d’être malade. Quand ton père viendra te rendre visite, dis-lui : “Je t’en prie, permets à ma sœur Tamar de venir me donner à manger. Qu’elle prépare le repas ici, devant moi, pour que je la regarde faire et que je mange ensuite de sa main.” »
fr.R: Jonadab lui a dit : « Va te coucher et fais comme si tu étais malade. Ton père viendra voir comment tu vas. Demande-lui : “Est-ce que ma sœur Tamar pourrait venir m’apporter quelque chose à manger ? Je voudrais qu’elle prépare le repas ici, pour que je la regarde. Ensuite, je mangerai ce qu’elle me donnera de sa main.” »

vi.L: Giô-na-đáp nói với chàng: "Hãy nằm trên giường của anh và giả bệnh. Khi cha anh đến thăm anh, anh hãy nói với người: 'Xin cho Ta-ma em gái con đến, cho con ăn, và để nàng làm món ăn trước mắt con, để con thấy và ăn từ tay nàng.'"
vi.B: Giô-na-đáp bảo chàng: "Anh cứ nằm trên giường và giả vờ đau ốm. Khi cha anh đến thăm, anh hãy thưa với người: 'Xin cha cho Ta-ma em gái con đến đút cho con ăn. Xin cho em ấy làm món ăn ngay trước mặt con, để con nhìn thấy rồi ăn từ tay em ấy.'"
vi.R: Giô-na-đáp bảo: "Anh hãy lên giường nằm và làm như mình đang bệnh. Cha anh sẽ đến thăm anh. Lúc đó anh hãy xin: 'Cha cho Ta-ma em gái con đến mang cho con chút gì ăn được không? Con muốn em ấy nấu ngay ở đây cho con nhìn. Rồi con sẽ ăn từ tay em ấy.'"

decisions.choice: make yourself sick: pretend to be ill
decisions.reason: The same verb form as in verse 2, here plainly meaning to act the part of a sick man, as verse 6 confirms.

decisions.choice: give me food to eat; the food: a meal brought to someone sick or grieving
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun come from a root used of food given to the sick or the mourning (3:35; 12:17). A sick man asking for a meal from his sister's hand would not seem strange to the king.

decisions.choice: Jonadab: the Hebrew here spells the name in a longer form
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has Jehonadab, the full form of the name, with the divine name as its first part. It is the same man as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: Jonadab
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the spelling of verse 3, so that readers do not think a second man has come in.

decisions.choice: David's sons speak to him as "cha" and of themselves as "con"
decisions.reason: Amnon speaks to his father in a family matter; the Hebrew here has no "your servant", so the parent-and-child forms of the Genesis note are used. Where a son uses court language ("your servant", "the king"), the court forms are kept.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אַמְנ֖וֹן וַיִּתְחָ֑ל וַיָּבֹ֨א הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לִרְאֹת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַמְנ֤וֹן אֶל־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ תָּֽבוֹא־נָ֞א תָּמָ֣ר אֲחֹתִ֗י וּתְלַבֵּ֤ב לְעֵינַי֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י לְבִב֔וֹת וְאֶבְרֶ֖ה מִיָּדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Amnon and made himself sick, and came the king to see him, and said Amnon to the king, let come please Tamar my sister and let her make cakes before my eyes, two cakes, and I will eat from her hand.

en.L: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. And the king came to see him, and Amnon said to the king, "Please let Tamar my sister come and make two cakes in my sight, and I will eat from her hand."
en.B: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to him, "I beg you, let my sister Tamar come here and make a couple of cakes in front of me, so that I can eat from her hand."
en.R: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. The king came to visit him, and Amnon said, "Please send my sister Tamar to me. Let her make two cakes while I watch. Then I can eat them from her hand."

es.L: Y Amnón se acostó y fingió estar enfermo. Y el rey vino a verlo, y Amnón dijo al rey: «Te ruego que venga Tamar mi hermana y haga dos tortas ante mis ojos, y comeré de su mano».
es.B: Así que Amnón se acostó y fingió estar enfermo. Cuando el rey vino a verlo, Amnón le dijo: «Te suplico que dejes venir a mi hermana Tamar para que haga aquí delante de mí un par de tortas, y yo las coma de su mano».
es.R: Entonces Amnón se metió en la cama y fingió estar enfermo. El rey vino a visitarlo, y Amnón le dijo: «Por favor, envíame a mi hermana Tamar. Que haga dos tortas mientras yo la miro. Así podré comerlas de su mano».

fr.L: Et Amnon se coucha et fit le malade. Et le roi vint le voir, et Amnon dit au roi : « Que Tamar ma sœur vienne, je te prie, et qu’elle fasse sous mes yeux deux gâteaux, et je mangerai de sa main. »
fr.B: Amnon se coucha donc et fit semblant d’être malade. Quand le roi vint le voir, Amnon lui dit : « Je t’en prie, laisse ma sœur Tamar venir ici préparer devant moi quelques gâteaux, pour que je mange de sa main. »
fr.R: Amnon s’est donc mis au lit et a fait semblant d’être malade. Le roi est venu le voir, et Amnon lui a dit : « S’il te plaît, envoie-moi ma sœur Tamar. Qu’elle fasse deux gâteaux pendant que je la regarde. Ensuite, je les mangerai de sa main. »

vi.L: Vậy Am-nôn nằm xuống và giả bệnh. Vua đến thăm chàng, và Am-nôn nói với vua: "Xin cho Ta-ma em gái con đến và làm hai cái bánh trước mắt con, rồi con sẽ ăn từ tay nàng."
vi.B: Vậy Am-nôn nằm xuống giả vờ đau ốm. Khi vua đến thăm, Am-nôn thưa với vua: "Con xin cha cho Ta-ma em gái con đến đây làm vài cái bánh trước mặt con, để con được ăn từ tay em ấy."
vi.R: Vậy Am-nôn lên giường nằm và giả bệnh. Vua đến thăm chàng. Am-nôn thưa: "Xin cha cho Ta-ma em gái con đến với con. Xin cho em ấy làm hai cái bánh trong khi con nhìn. Rồi con sẽ ăn bánh từ tay em ấy."

decisions.choice: make cakes; cakes: a kind of cake, perhaps heart-shaped
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun are built from the word for "heart", and are found only in this story. They may name heart-shaped cakes, or cakes thought to give strength. Elsewhere the same verb means "you have captured my heart" (Song of Songs 4:9), so the words may also hint at Amnon's desire.

decisions.choice: two cakes: a small amount
decisions.reason: Asking for just two cakes makes the request sound modest and harmless.

decisions.choice: a couple of cakes
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the small number; Literal and Readable keep "two".

decisions.choice: Amnon says "tu" to the king, his father
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: one person is "tu" at every level, the king included; respect is carried by "je te prie", "mon seigneur le roi" and "ton serviteur". This holds for the whole block.

decisions.choice: tortas
decisions.reason: The Hebrew cakes are a kind found only in this story (m1); 'tortas' is the plain Spanish word for flat cakes of dough, and says no more about their shape than the Hebrew does.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֛ד אֶל־תָּמָ֖ר הַבַּ֣יְתָה לֵאמֹ֑ר לְכִ֣י נָ֗א בֵּ֚ית אַמְנ֣וֹן אָחִ֔יךְ וַעֲשִׂי־ל֖וֹ הַבִּרְיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent David to Tamar to the house, saying, go please [to the] house of Amnon your brother and make for him the food.

en.L: And David sent to Tamar at the house, saying, "Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare the food for him."
en.B: David sent word to Tamar at the palace: "Please go to your brother Amnon's house and prepare some food for him."
en.R: So David sent a message to Tamar at the palace. It said, "Please go to your brother Amnon's house and make some food for him."

es.L: Y David envió a decir a Tamar, a la casa: «Te ruego que vayas a la casa de Amnón tu hermano y le prepares la comida».
es.B: David mandó decir a Tamar en el palacio: «Por favor, ve a casa de tu hermano Amnón y prepárale algo de comer».
es.R: Entonces David le envió un mensaje a Tamar al palacio. Decía: «Por favor, ve a casa de tu hermano Amnón y hazle algo de comer».

fr.L: Et David envoya [dire] à Tamar, à la maison : « Va, je te prie, à la maison d’Amnon ton frère, et prépare-lui la nourriture. »
fr.B: David fit dire à Tamar, au palais : « Va, je te prie, chez ton frère Amnon et prépare-lui quelque chose à manger. »
fr.R: Alors David a envoyé un message à Tamar, au palais : « S’il te plaît, va chez ton frère Amnon et prépare-lui quelque chose à manger. »

vi.L: Đa-vít sai [người] đến nhà với Ta-ma mà nói: "Xin con hãy đi đến nhà Am-nôn anh con và làm món ăn cho anh ấy."
vi.B: Đa-vít sai người vào cung báo cho Ta-ma: "Con hãy đến nhà Am-nôn anh con và nấu chút gì cho anh ấy ăn."
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít sai người vào cung nói với Ta-ma: "Con hãy đến nhà Am-nôn anh con và nấu cho anh ấy chút gì để ăn."

decisions.choice: the house: the royal palace
decisions.reason: "The house" here is the king's house, where Tamar lived. The king's grown sons had houses of their own (verse 8; 14:24).

decisions.choice: David sent: the king himself sends her
decisions.reason: The plan works through David's own order. He does not suspect anything, and Tamar goes because her father has told her to.

decisions.choice: the palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "palace" for "the house", since it was the king's.

source.text: וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ תָּמָ֗ר בֵּ֛ית אַמְנ֥וֹן אָחִ֖יהָ וְה֣וּא שֹׁכֵ֑ב וַתִּקַּ֨ח אֶת־הַבָּצֵ֤ק וַתָּ֨לָשׁ֙ וַתְּלַבֵּ֣ב לְעֵינָ֔יו וַתְּבַשֵּׁ֖ל אֶת־הַלְּבִבֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Tamar [to the] house of Amnon her brother, and he [was] lying down; and she took the dough and kneaded and made cakes before his eyes, and baked the cakes.

en.L: And Tamar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he [was] lying down. And she took the dough and kneaded [it] and made cakes in his sight and baked the cakes.
en.B: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house, where he was lying in bed. She took dough, kneaded it, made cakes while he watched, and baked them.
en.R: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon's house. He was lying in bed. She took some dough and kneaded it. She shaped it into cakes while he watched, and she cooked them.

es.L: Y Tamar fue a la casa de Amnón su hermano, y él [estaba] acostado. Y tomó la masa y [la] amasó, e hizo tortas ante sus ojos, y coció las tortas.
es.B: Tamar fue a casa de su hermano Amnón, que estaba acostado en la cama. Tomó masa, la amasó, hizo las tortas mientras él miraba, y las coció.
es.R: Tamar fue a casa de su hermano Amnón. Él estaba acostado en la cama. Ella tomó un poco de masa y la amasó. Le dio forma de tortas mientras él la miraba, y las coció.

fr.L: Et Tamar alla à la maison d’Amnon son frère, et il [était] couché ; et elle prit la pâte, et la pétrit, et fit des gâteaux sous ses yeux, et fit cuire les gâteaux.
fr.B: Tamar se rendit donc chez son frère Amnon, qui était couché. Elle prit de la pâte, la pétrit, façonna des gâteaux sous ses yeux et les fit cuire.
fr.R: Tamar est donc allée chez son frère Amnon. Il était couché. Elle a pris de la pâte et l’a pétrie. Elle en a fait des gâteaux pendant qu’il la regardait, et elle les a fait cuire.

vi.L: Ta-ma đi đến nhà Am-nôn anh mình, và chàng đang nằm. Nàng lấy bột, nhồi, làm bánh trước mắt chàng và nướng bánh.
vi.B: Vậy Ta-ma đến nhà Am-nôn anh mình, lúc ấy chàng đang nằm trên giường. Nàng lấy bột nhồi, nặn bánh trước mặt chàng rồi nướng bánh.
vi.R: Vậy Ta-ma đến nhà Am-nôn anh mình. Chàng đang nằm trên giường. Nàng lấy một ít bột và nhồi. Nàng nặn bột thành bánh trong khi chàng nhìn, rồi nướng bánh.

decisions.choice: baked: cooked
decisions.reason: The verb means to cook in general, by boiling or baking. With cakes of dough, baking or frying is meant.

decisions.choice: kneaded: the written and the read forms differ only in spelling
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this verb one way in its letters and its scribes' notes read it another way. Both forms mean "she kneaded"; nothing in the sense changes.

decisions.choice: she took, kneaded, made, baked: each step told
decisions.reason: The run of short verbs slows the story and shows Tamar doing all that she was asked, in full view of Amnon.

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הַמַּשְׂרֵת֙ וַתִּצֹ֣ק לְפָנָ֔יו וַיְמָאֵ֖ן לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַמְנ֗וֹן הוֹצִ֤יאוּ כָל־אִישׁ֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י וַיֵּצְא֥וּ כָל־אִ֖ישׁ מֵעָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And she took the pan and poured out before him, and he refused to eat; and said Amnon, send out every man from with me; and went out every man from with him.

en.L: And she took the pan and poured [them] out before him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Send everyone out from me." And everyone went out from him.
en.B: Then she took the pan and set the cakes out before him, but he refused to eat. "Send everyone out of here," Amnon said, and they all left him.
en.R: Then she took the pan and served him the cakes, but he would not eat. Amnon said, "Make everyone leave!" So everyone went out.

es.L: Y tomó la sartén y [las] vació delante de él, pero él se negó a comer. Y Amnón dijo: «{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} salir a todos de mi lado». Y salieron todos de su lado.
es.B: Luego tomó la sartén y le sirvió las tortas delante de él, pero él se negó a comer. «Que salgan todos de aquí», dijo Amnón, y todos lo dejaron.
es.R: Luego tomó la sartén y le sirvió las tortas, pero él no quiso comer. Amnón dijo: «¡Que se vayan todos!». Y todos salieron.

fr.L: Et elle prit la poêle et [les] versa devant lui, mais il refusa de manger. Et Amnon dit : « Faites sortir tout le monde d’auprès de moi. » Et tout le monde sortit d’auprès de lui.
fr.B: Puis elle prit la poêle et disposa les gâteaux devant lui, mais il refusa de manger. « Faites sortir tout le monde d’ici », dit Amnon ; et tous le laissèrent.
fr.R: Ensuite, elle a pris la poêle et lui a servi les gâteaux, mais il n’a pas voulu manger. Amnon a dit : « Faites sortir tout le monde ! » Alors tout le monde est sorti.

vi.L: Nàng lấy chảo và đổ [bánh] ra trước mặt chàng, nhưng chàng không chịu ăn. Am-nôn nói: "Hãy cho mọi người ra khỏi chỗ ta." Mọi người đều ra khỏi chỗ chàng.
vi.B: Rồi nàng lấy chảo, trút bánh ra trước mặt chàng, nhưng chàng không chịu ăn. Am-nôn nói: "Cho mọi người ra khỏi đây." Thế là mọi người đều ra ngoài.
vi.R: Rồi nàng lấy chảo và dọn bánh cho chàng, nhưng chàng không ăn. Am-nôn nói: "Bảo mọi người ra ngoài hết!" Vậy mọi người đều đi ra.

decisions.choice: the pan; poured out: she tipped the cakes out of the pan
decisions.reason: The word for the pan is found only here, so its exact shape is not known. "Poured out" suggests she turned the cakes out of it in front of him.

decisions.choice: send everyone out from me: the words Joseph used
decisions.reason: Joseph gave the same order before he made himself known to his brothers (Genesis 45:1). There it cleared the room for a family reunion; here it clears the room for a crime against a sister.

decisions.choice: every man: everyone present
decisions.reason: The phrase means every person there, chiefly the servants. Tamar is left alone with Amnon.

decisions.choice: set the cakes out (Balanced); served him the cakes (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name what she poured out; Balanced and Readable name the cakes.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַמְנ֜וֹן אֶל־תָּמָ֗ר הָבִ֤יאִי הַבִּרְיָה֙ הַחֶ֔דֶר וְאֶבְרֶ֖ה מִיָּדֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֣ח תָּמָ֗ר אֶת־הַלְּבִבוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔תָה וַתָּבֵ֛א לְאַמְנ֥וֹן אָחִ֖יהָ הֶחָֽדְרָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Amnon to Tamar, bring the food [into] the chamber, and I will eat from your hand. And took Tamar the cakes which she had made and brought [them] to Amnon her brother to the chamber.

en.L: And Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner room, so that I may eat from your hand." And Tamar took the cakes that she had made and brought [them] to Amnon her brother into the inner room.
en.B: Amnon then told Tamar, "Bring the food in here to the bedroom, and I will eat from your hand." So Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to her brother Amnon in the bedroom.
en.R: Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into my bedroom. I want you to feed me." So Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to her brother Amnon in his bedroom.

es.L: Y Amnón dijo a Tamar: «Trae la comida a la alcoba, para que yo coma de tu mano». Y Tamar tomó las tortas que había hecho y [las] llevó a Amnón su hermano, a la alcoba.
es.B: Entonces Amnón le dijo a Tamar: «Trae la comida aquí al dormitorio, y comeré de tu mano». Tamar tomó las tortas que había hecho y se las llevó a su hermano Amnón al dormitorio.
es.R: Entonces Amnón le dijo a Tamar: «Trae la comida a mi dormitorio. Quiero que tú me des de comer». Tamar tomó las tortas que había hecho y se las llevó a su hermano Amnón a su dormitorio.

fr.L: Et Amnon dit à Tamar : « Apporte la nourriture dans la chambre, et je mangerai de ta main. » Et Tamar prit les gâteaux qu’elle avait faits et [les] apporta à Amnon son frère dans la chambre.
fr.B: Amnon dit alors à Tamar : « Apporte le repas ici, dans la chambre, et je mangerai de ta main. » Tamar prit les gâteaux qu’elle avait préparés et les apporta à son frère Amnon dans la chambre.
fr.R: Puis Amnon a dit à Tamar : « Apporte le repas dans ma chambre. Je veux que tu me donnes à manger. » Tamar a donc pris les gâteaux qu’elle avait faits et les a apportés à son frère Amnon, dans sa chambre.

vi.L: Am-nôn nói với Ta-ma: "Hãy đem món ăn vào phòng trong, để anh ăn từ tay em." Ta-ma lấy những cái bánh nàng đã làm và đem vào phòng trong cho Am-nôn anh mình.
vi.B: Am-nôn bảo Ta-ma: "Em đem món ăn vào phòng ngủ đây, để anh ăn từ tay em." Ta-ma lấy những cái bánh mình đã làm, đem vào phòng ngủ cho Am-nôn anh mình.
vi.R: Rồi Am-nôn nói với Ta-ma: "Em đem thức ăn vào phòng ngủ của anh. Anh muốn em đút cho anh ăn." Vậy Ta-ma lấy những cái bánh mình đã làm và đem vào phòng ngủ cho Am-nôn anh mình.

decisions.choice: the chamber: an inner, private room, here his bedroom
decisions.reason: The word names a room further inside a house, out of sight (Genesis 43:30). With Amnon lying sick, it is the room where he slept (Exodus 7:28 speaks of a "bedroom" with the same word).

decisions.choice: Amnon her brother: the narrator keeps calling him her brother
decisions.reason: "Her brother" is repeated through the story (verses 4, 7, 8, 10, 12). The repetition makes plain the bond Amnon is about to violate.

decisions.choice: the bedroom
decisions.reason: Literal says "inner room", the general sense; Balanced and Readable say "bedroom", the room meant here. Readable puts "eat from your hand" as "feed me".

decisions.choice: la alcoba (L); el dormitorio (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses 'alcoba', an inner private room, for the general sense (m1); Balanced and Readable name the room meant here, 'dormitorio', as the English says 'bedroom'.

source.text: וַתַּגֵּ֥שׁ אֵלָ֖יו לֶֽאֱכֹ֑ל וַיַּֽחֲזֶק־בָּהּ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֔הּ בּ֛וֹאִי שִׁכְבִ֥י עִמִּ֖י אֲחוֹתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she brought [them] near to him to eat, and he seized her and said to her, come, lie with me, my sister.

en.L: And she brought [them] near to him to eat, and he seized her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
en.B: But when she brought them close for him to eat, he grabbed her and said to her, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
en.R: But when she held the food out to him, he grabbed her. He said, "Come to bed with me, my sister."

es.L: Y ella [se las] acercó para que comiera, y él la agarró y le dijo: «Ven, acuéstate conmigo, hermana mía».
es.B: Pero cuando ella se las acercó para que comiera, él la agarró y le dijo: «Ven, acuéstate conmigo, hermana mía».
es.R: Pero cuando ella le acercó la comida, él la agarró. Le dijo: «Ven a la cama conmigo, hermana mía».

fr.L: Et elle [les] lui présenta pour qu’il mange, et il la saisit et lui dit : « Viens, couche avec moi, ma sœur. »
fr.B: Mais quand elle les approcha de lui pour qu’il mange, il l’empoigna et lui dit : « Viens, couche avec moi, ma sœur. »
fr.R: Mais quand elle lui a tendu la nourriture, il l’a attrapée. Il lui a dit : « Viens au lit avec moi, ma sœur. »

vi.L: Nàng đem [bánh] đến gần chàng để chàng ăn, thì chàng nắm lấy nàng và nói với nàng: "Hãy đến nằm với anh, em gái của anh."
vi.B: Nhưng khi nàng đưa bánh đến gần cho chàng ăn, chàng nắm chặt lấy nàng và nói: "Em gái của anh, hãy đến nằm với anh."
vi.R: Nhưng khi nàng đưa thức ăn cho chàng, chàng chụp lấy nàng và nói: "Em gái của anh, hãy lên giường với anh."

decisions.choice: seized her: took hold of her by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to grasp firmly. It is the verb of the law on a man who seizes a woman in the countryside (Deuteronomy 22:25).

decisions.choice: come, lie with me: the words of Potiphar's wife
decisions.reason: Potiphar's wife said the same words when she seized Joseph (Genesis 39:7, 12). Joseph got away; Tamar cannot.

decisions.choice: my sister: the relationship the law forbade
decisions.reason: The law forbade sexual relations with a sister or half-sister (Leviticus 18:9, 11; 20:17; Deuteronomy 27:22). Amnon calls her "my sister" in the very words that ask for what the law forbids.

decisions.choice: Come to bed with me
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what Amnon is asking, in words that a young reader can follow without being graphic.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אַל־אָחִי֙ אַל־תְּעַנֵּ֔נִי כִּ֛י לֹא־יֵֽעָשֶׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַֽל־תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה אֶת־הַנְּבָלָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to him, no, my brother, do not humble me, for not it is done thus in Israel; do not do the disgraceful thing, this.

en.L: And she said to him, "No, my brother! Do not humble me, for such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing.
en.B: "No, my brother!" she said to him. "Do not violate me! Such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not do this outrageous thing.
en.R: "No, my brother!" she said. "Do not force me! A thing like this must never be done in Israel. Do not do this shameful thing.

es.L: Y ella le dijo: «¡No, hermano mío! No me humilles, porque no se hace así en Israel. No cometas esta infamia.
es.B: «¡No, hermano mío!», le dijo ella. «¡No me deshonres! Eso no se hace en Israel. No cometas esta atrocidad.
es.R: «¡No, hermano mío!», le dijo ella. «¡No me fuerces! Algo así no debe hacerse nunca en Israel. No hagas esta cosa tan vergonzosa.

fr.L: Et elle lui dit : « Non, mon frère ! Ne m’humilie pas, car cela ne se fait pas en Israël. Ne commets pas cette infamie.
fr.B: « Non, mon frère ! lui dit-elle. Ne me fais pas violence ! Cela ne se fait pas en Israël. Ne commets pas cette infamie.
fr.R: « Non, mon frère ! a-t-elle dit. Ne me force pas ! Une chose pareille ne doit jamais se faire en Israël. Ne fais pas cette chose honteuse.

vi.L: Nàng nói với chàng: "Không, anh ơi! Đừng làm nhục em, vì không ai làm như thế trong Y-sơ-ra-ên. Đừng làm điều ô nhục này.
vi.B: Nàng nói: "Không, anh ơi! Đừng cưỡng bức em! Trong Y-sơ-ra-ên không ai làm chuyện như thế. Đừng làm điều đồi bại này.
vi.R: Nàng nói: "Không, anh ơi! Đừng ép em! Trong Y-sơ-ra-ên không bao giờ được làm chuyện như thế. Đừng làm điều đáng xấu hổ này.

decisions.choice: humble me: violate me, take my honor by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to humble, degrade or violate. It is used of the rape of Dinah (Genesis 34:2) and in the law on a man who seizes a woman (Deuteronomy 22:29). Here it names the wrong Amnon is about to do to her; it returns in verses 14, 22 and 32.

decisions.choice: disgraceful thing: an outrage that shames the whole people
decisions.reason: The word is used of a gross wrong, often a sexual one, that breaks the bonds of the community: the rape of Dinah (Genesis 34:7), the outrage at Gibeah (Judges 19:23; 20:6) and the case in Deuteronomy 22:21.

decisions.choice: it is not done thus in Israel: Tamar appeals to the people's own standard
decisions.reason: Her words echo what Jacob's sons said after Dinah was raped: "such a thing is not done" (Genesis 34:7). Tamar reminds Amnon that this is not just a private act but a crime against Israel's way of life.

decisions.choice: humble (Literal); violate (Balanced); force (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "humble" and Balanced says "violate", as in Deuteronomy 22:29, where a man also takes hold of the woman. Readable says "force" here, and "rape" when the act is told (verses 14, 22, 32), since the story makes plain that force was used (as Judges 20:5 says "raped"); Deuteronomy 22 says "dishonored" at Readable, where the law covers more than one case.

decisions.choice: outrageous thing (Balanced); shameful thing (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 22:21, Balanced says "outrageous" and Readable says "shameful". Literal keeps "disgraceful", as in Genesis 34:7.

decisions.choice: "humilier" (L); "faire violence" (B); "forcer" (R)
decisions.reason: The same verb is followed through the chapter: Literal keeps the Hebrew image, Balanced and Readable say what is meant (m1), as the English does with "humble", "violate", "force".

decisions.choice: humillar (L); deshonrar (B); forzar (R), and 'violar' at R where the act is told (verses 14, 22, 32)
decisions.reason: As the English decision (r-en-1): Literal keeps the Hebrew verb's 'humble'; Balanced says 'deshonrar', the wrong done to her honor; Readable says 'forzar' here and 'violar' where the act is told, since the story makes plain that force was used.

decisions.choice: infamia (L); atrocidad (B); cosa tan vergonzosa (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word names an outrage that shames the whole people (m2). Spanish 'infamia' keeps the disgrace at Literal; Balanced 'atrocidad' follows the English 'outrageous thing'; Readable says plainly that it is shameful.

decisions.choice: "làm nhục" (L); "cưỡng bức" (B); "ép" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to humble or violate (meaning decision). Literal keeps the sense of shaming, Balanced names the force, and Readable keeps a plain word that a young reader can follow without being graphic, as the English does.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י אָ֤נָה אוֹלִיךְ֙ אֶת־חֶרְפָּתִ֔י וְאַתָּ֗ה תִּהְיֶ֛ה כְּאַחַ֥ד הַנְּבָלִ֖ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּה֙ דַּבֶּר־נָ֣א אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִמְנָעֵ֖נִי מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, where will I carry my disgrace? And you, you will be like one of the fools in Israel. And now speak please to the king, for not will he withhold me from you.

en.L: And I, where would I carry my disgrace? And you, you would be like one of the disgraceful fools in Israel. And now, please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you."
en.B: As for me, where could I go with my shame? And you would be counted among the outrageous fools in Israel. Now please, speak to the king. He will not keep me from you."
en.R: Where could I go? I would have to live with this disgrace. And people would think of you as one of the worst fools in Israel. Please, just talk to the king. He will let you marry me."

es.L: Y yo, ¿adónde llevaría mi deshonra? Y tú, tú serías como uno de los infames necios de Israel. Y ahora, te ruego que hables al rey, porque él no me negará a ti».
es.B: En cuanto a mí, ¿adónde podría ir con mi vergüenza? Y tú serías contado entre los infames necios de Israel. Ahora, por favor, habla con el rey. Él no me negará a ti».
es.R: ¿Adónde podría ir yo? Tendría que vivir con esta vergüenza. Y la gente te tendría por uno de los peores necios de Israel. Por favor, simplemente habla con el rey. Él te dejará casarte conmigo».

fr.L: Et moi, où porterais-je ma honte ? Et toi, tu serais comme l’un des insensés en Israël. Et maintenant, parle donc au roi, car il ne me refusera pas à toi. »
fr.B: Moi, où irais-je avec ma honte ? Et toi, tu passerais pour l’un des pires insensés d’Israël. Maintenant, je t’en prie, parle au roi. Il ne refusera pas de me donner à toi. »
fr.R: Où pourrais-je aller ? Je devrais vivre avec cette honte. Et les gens te regarderaient comme l’un des pires insensés d’Israël. S’il te plaît, parle simplement au roi. Il te permettra de m’épouser. »

vi.L: Còn em, em sẽ mang nỗi nhục của em đi đâu? Còn anh, anh sẽ như một trong những kẻ đồi bại trong Y-sơ-ra-ên. Vậy bây giờ, xin anh hãy nói với vua, vì vua sẽ không giữ em lại không cho anh đâu."
vi.B: Còn em, em biết mang nỗi nhục này đi đâu? Còn anh, anh sẽ bị xem như một kẻ đồi bại trong Y-sơ-ra-ên. Bây giờ, xin anh hãy nói với vua. Vua sẽ không từ chối gả em cho anh đâu."
vi.R: Em biết đi đâu bây giờ? Em sẽ phải sống với nỗi nhục này suốt đời. Còn anh, người ta sẽ coi anh là một trong những kẻ ngu xuẩn tệ hại nhất trong Y-sơ-ra-ên. Xin anh cứ nói với vua. Vua sẽ cho anh cưới em."

decisions.choice: where would I carry my disgrace: there would be nowhere I could go with my shame
decisions.reason: The question expects no answer. A woman raped and then left unmarried bore a shame that would follow her for life; verse 20 shows that this is what happened.

decisions.choice: the fools: people who are morally reckless and shameless
decisions.reason: The word is related to "disgraceful thing" in verse 12. It does not mean dull or slow, but someone who acts without regard for God or for others, like Nabal, whose name means "fool" (1 Samuel 25:25). Amnon, the heir to the throne, would be counted among the worst of men.

decisions.choice: he will not withhold me from you: the king would let you marry me
decisions.reason: The law forbade marriage with a half-sister (Leviticus 18:9, 11; 20:17), though in the time of the ancestors Abraham had married his (Genesis 20:12). The text does not say whether Tamar thought David would really allow it or was saying anything she could to escape. Either way, she offers Amnon a lawful way and he refuses it.

decisions.choice: I would have to live with this disgrace; He will let you marry me
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the question into a question and a statement of what it implies, and says plainly that "he will not withhold me from you" means marriage.

decisions.choice: "kẻ đồi bại" (L, B); "kẻ ngu xuẩn tệ hại nhất" (R) for "the fools"
decisions.reason: The word means someone morally shameless, not slow-witted (meaning decision), so Literal and Balanced use "đồi bại", which echoes "điều đồi bại" of verse 12 in Balanced; Readable follows the English "the worst fools".

source.text: וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ בְּקוֹלָ֑הּ וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק מִמֶּ֨נָּה֙ וַיְעַנֶּ֔הָ וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב אֹתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But not he was willing to listen to her voice, and he was stronger than her, and he humbled her and lay her.

en.L: But he was not willing to listen to her voice; and he was stronger than she, and he humbled her and lay with her.
en.B: But he would not listen to her. He was stronger than she was, and he violated her and lay with her by force.
en.R: But Amnon would not listen to her. He was stronger than she was, and he raped her.

es.L: Pero él no quiso escuchar su voz; y siendo más fuerte que ella, la humilló y se acostó con ella.
es.B: Pero él no quiso escucharla. Era más fuerte que ella, y la deshonró y se acostó con ella por la fuerza.
es.R: Pero Amnón no quiso escucharla. Era más fuerte que ella, y la violó.

fr.L: Mais il ne voulut pas écouter sa voix ; et il fut plus fort qu’elle, et il l’humilia et coucha avec elle.
fr.B: Mais il ne voulut pas l’écouter. Il était plus fort qu’elle ; il lui fit violence et coucha avec elle de force.
fr.R: Mais Amnon n’a pas voulu l’écouter. Il était plus fort qu’elle, et il l’a violée.

vi.L: Nhưng chàng không muốn nghe tiếng nàng; chàng mạnh hơn nàng, chàng làm nhục nàng và nằm với nàng.
vi.B: Nhưng chàng không chịu nghe nàng. Chàng mạnh hơn nàng, nên đã cưỡng bức nàng và nằm với nàng.
vi.R: Nhưng Am-nôn không chịu nghe Ta-ma. Chàng mạnh hơn nàng, và chàng đã cưỡng hiếp nàng.

decisions.choice: he was stronger than she: he overpowered her
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 11, "he seized her", here with "than her": he used his strength against her. The text leaves no doubt that she did not consent.

decisions.choice: humbled her and lay her: he raped her
decisions.reason: The verb "humble" is the one of verse 12. "Lay her" is written with the mark of a direct object instead of the usual "lay with her", as in the rape of Dinah (Genesis 34:2); the wording presents her as acted upon, not as a partner. Together the verbs describe rape, as in Deuteronomy 22:25.

decisions.choice: he was not willing to listen to her voice: her plea is refused
decisions.reason: Tamar had spoken at length (verses 12-13); Amnon does not answer her. The same words return in verse 16, when he refuses to listen a second time.

decisions.choice: violated her and lay with her by force (Balanced); raped her (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verbs. Balanced keeps "violated" for the verb of verse 12 and adds "by force" for the wording of "lay her" and the overpowering just described. Readable says in one plain word what the verbs together describe. The text tells the act soberly, and the English does the same.

source.text: וַיִּשְׂנָאֶ֣הָ אַמְנ֗וֹן שִׂנְאָה֙ גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י גְדוֹלָ֗ה הַשִּׂנְאָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שְׂנֵאָ֔הּ מֵאַהֲבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲהֵבָ֑הּ וַֽיֹּאמֶר־לָ֥הּ אַמְנ֖וֹן ק֥וּמִי לֵֽכִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And hated her Amnon [with] hatred great very, for greater [was] the hatred which he hated her than the love which he had loved her. And said to her Amnon, get up, go.

en.L: And Amnon hated her [with] a very great hatred, for the hatred with which he hated her [was] greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, "Get up, go!"
en.B: Then Amnon turned on her with a fierce hatred. What he felt against her now was stronger than the love he had once felt for her. "Get up and go!" Amnon said to her.
en.R: Then Amnon began to hate Tamar bitterly. His hatred for her was even stronger than his love had been. He said to her, "Get up and get out!"

es.L: Y Amnón la odió [con] un odio muy grande, porque el odio con que la odió [fue] mayor que el amor con que la había amado. Y Amnón le dijo: «¡Levántate, vete!».
es.B: Entonces Amnón se volvió contra ella con un odio feroz. Lo que ahora sentía contra ella era más fuerte que el amor que antes le había tenido. «¡Levántate y vete!», le dijo Amnón.
es.R: Entonces Amnón empezó a odiar a Tamar con amargura. Su odio por ella era aún más fuerte de lo que había sido su amor. Le dijo: «¡Levántate y lárgate!».

fr.L: Et Amnon la haït d’une très grande haine, car la haine dont il la haït [fut] plus grande que l’amour dont il l’avait aimée. Et Amnon lui dit : « Lève-toi, va-t’en ! »
fr.B: Alors Amnon se mit à la haïr violemment. La haine qu’il éprouvait maintenant pour elle était plus forte que l’amour qu’il avait eu pour elle. « Lève-toi et va-t’en ! » lui dit Amnon.
fr.R: Ensuite, Amnon s’est mis à détester Tamar profondément. Sa haine pour elle était encore plus forte que son amour d’avant. Il lui a dit : « Lève-toi et sors d’ici ! »

vi.L: Rồi Am-nôn ghét nàng [với] một sự ghét rất lớn, vì sự ghét mà chàng ghét nàng [thì] lớn hơn tình yêu mà chàng đã yêu nàng. Am-nôn nói với nàng: "Đứng dậy, đi đi!"
vi.B: Rồi Am-nôn quay ra căm ghét nàng dữ dội. Lòng căm ghét chàng dành cho nàng bây giờ còn mạnh hơn tình yêu chàng đã dành cho nàng trước đó. Am-nôn bảo nàng: "Đứng dậy, đi đi!"
vi.R: Sau đó Am-nôn bắt đầu ghét Ta-ma cay đắng. Chàng ghét nàng còn hơn lúc trước chàng yêu nàng. Chàng nói với nàng: "Đứng dậy, cút đi!"

decisions.choice: hated her with a very great hatred: the hatred is stressed
decisions.reason: The words "hate" and "hatred" come four times in the verse, "love" twice. The repetition shows how completely Amnon's desire has turned to loathing.

decisions.choice: the love with which he had loved her: his desire for her
decisions.reason: The love of verse 1 is shown to have been desire, which ended once he had used her.

decisions.choice: get up, go: a curt dismissal
decisions.reason: Two bare commands, without her name or any courtesy. He speaks to her as one would drive off someone unwanted.

decisions.choice: What he felt against her now was stronger than the love he had once felt
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable shorten the repeated "hatred with which he hated her" so the comparison reads clearly; Literal keeps the repetition. Readable says "get out" for the second command, its sense here.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אַל־אוֹדֹ֞ת הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את מֵאַחֶ֛רֶת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֥יתָ עִמִּ֖י לְשַׁלְּחֵ֑נִי וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לִשְׁמֹ֥עַֽ לָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to him, no, because of this great evil, more than [the] other which you did with me, to send me away. But not he was willing to listen to her.

en.L: And she said to him, "No! For this great wrong, sending me away, [is worse] than the other that you have done to me." But he was not willing to listen to her.
en.B: "No!" she said to him. "Sending me away would be a greater wrong than what you have already done to me." But he would not listen to her.
en.R: "No!" she said. "Sending me away is even worse than what you have already done to me." But he would not listen to her.

es.L: Y ella le dijo: «¡No! Porque este gran mal, echarme, [es peor] que el otro que me has hecho». Pero él no quiso escucharla.
es.B: «¡No!», le dijo ella. «Echarme ahora sería un mal mayor que el que ya me has hecho». Pero él no quiso escucharla.
es.R: «¡No!», le dijo ella. «Echarme ahora es todavía peor que lo que ya me has hecho». Pero él no quiso escucharla.

fr.L: Et elle lui dit : « Non ! Car ce grand mal, me renvoyer, [est pire] que l’autre que tu m’as fait. » Mais il ne voulut pas l’écouter.
fr.B: « Non ! lui dit-elle. Me renvoyer serait un mal plus grand encore que celui que tu viens de me faire. » Mais il ne voulut pas l’écouter.
fr.R: « Non ! a-t-elle dit. Me chasser maintenant, c’est encore pire que ce que tu m’as déjà fait. » Mais il n’a pas voulu l’écouter.

vi.L: Nàng nói với chàng: "Không! Vì điều sai trái lớn này, là đuổi em đi, [còn tệ hơn] điều kia anh đã làm với em." Nhưng chàng không muốn nghe nàng.
vi.B: Nàng nói: "Không! Đuổi em đi lúc này còn là tội lớn hơn điều anh vừa làm với em." Nhưng chàng không chịu nghe nàng.
vi.R: Nàng nói: "Không! Đuổi em đi còn tệ hơn điều anh vừa làm với em." Nhưng chàng không chịu nghe nàng.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text, read as: "No, for this great wrong of sending me away is worse than the other you did to me"
alternatives: No, brother, for this last wrong is greater than the first (ancient Greek)
decisions.reason: Tamar's words are hard to read in the Hebrew, as if spoken in distress, and the first words ("no, because of") do not fit together easily. The sense is clear enough: to send her away would be a greater wrong than the rape itself. The ancient Greek translation reads roughly "No, brother, for this last wrong is greater than the first", which may reflect a slightly different Hebrew text. The Hebrew is followed here; reviewers should check the Greek wording against an edition.

decisions.choice: to send me away: what the law forbade such a man to do
decisions.reason: The law said that a man who seized and lay with an unmarried girl must marry her and "may not send her away all his days" (Deuteronomy 22:29; see also Exodus 22:15). Amnon does the very thing the law forbade, and leaves her disgraced and without a husband. The verb returns in verse 17.

decisions.choice: he was not willing to listen to her: as in verse 14
decisions.reason: The narrator repeats the words of verse 14. A second time, her plea goes unheard.

decisions.choice: Sending me away would be a greater wrong
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the sending away at the front so the comparison is clear. Literal follows the Hebrew order and brackets "is worse", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶֽת־נַעֲרוֹ֙ מְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁלְחוּ־נָ֥א אֶת־זֹ֛את מֵעָלַ֖י הַח֑וּצָה וּנְעֹ֥ל הַדֶּ֖לֶת אַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he called his young man, his attendant, and said, send away please this from with me outside, and bolt the door after her.

en.L: And he called his young man who served him and said, "Please send this [woman] away from me, outside, and bolt the door after her."
en.B: He called the young man who attended him and said, "Put this woman out of my room, and bolt the door behind her."
en.R: He called his personal servant and said, "Get this woman out of here! Lock the door behind her!"

es.L: Y llamó a su joven que le servía y le dijo: «Te ruego que eches a esta [mujer] de mi lado, afuera, y cierra la puerta tras ella con cerrojo».
es.B: Llamó al joven que lo atendía y le dijo: «Saca a esta mujer de mi cuarto y echa el cerrojo a la puerta detrás de ella».
es.R: Llamó a su criado personal y le dijo: «¡Saca de aquí a esta mujer! ¡Cierra la puerta con llave detrás de ella!».

fr.L: Et il appela le jeune homme qui le servait et dit : « Renvoie donc celle-ci loin de moi, dehors, et verrouille la porte derrière elle. »
fr.B: Il appela le jeune homme qui était à son service et lui dit : « Mets cette femme hors de chez moi, et verrouille la porte derrière elle. »
fr.R: Il a appelé son serviteur personnel et lui a dit : « Fais sortir cette femme d’ici ! Ferme la porte à clé derrière elle ! »

vi.L: Chàng gọi người đầy tớ trẻ phục vụ mình mà nói: "Hãy đuổi [người đàn bà] này ra khỏi chỗ ta, ra bên ngoài, rồi cài then cửa sau lưng nó."
vi.B: Chàng gọi người đầy tớ trẻ hầu cận mình và nói: "Đuổi người đàn bà này ra khỏi phòng ta, rồi cài then cửa sau lưng nó."
vi.R: Chàng gọi người đầy tớ riêng của mình và nói: "Đuổi người đàn bà này ra khỏi đây! Khóa cửa lại sau lưng nó!"

decisions.choice: this: a word of contempt
decisions.reason: Amnon does not name her or call her his sister; he says only "this" (a feminine form, "this one"). The bare word shows his scorn.

decisions.choice: his young man who served him: his personal attendant
decisions.reason: The two words name a young man in his personal service. He is the only witness of how Tamar was thrown out.

decisions.choice: send away: the verb of verse 16
decisions.reason: Amnon gives the very order Tamar has just begged him not to give, and has his servant carry it out.

decisions.choice: Put this woman out of my room (Balanced); Get this woman out of here (Readable)
decisions.reason: The "please" in Amnon's order is a matter of form, and Balanced and Readable leave it out. "Woman" is supplied at every level for the bare "this", which English cannot use alone; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: "celle-ci"
decisions.reason: French has a feminine demonstrative pronoun that says "this one" with the same coldness as the Hebrew (m1), so Literal needs no bracketed noun.

decisions.choice: "nó" for Tamar in Amnon's mouth
decisions.reason: Amnon no longer names her or calls her sister; he says only "this" (meaning decision). The narrator keeps "nàng" for her; Amnon's "nó" carries his contempt.

source.text: וְעָלֶ֨יהָ֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת פַּסִּ֔ים כִּי֩ כֵ֨ן תִּלְבַּ֧שְׁןָ בְנוֹת־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ הַבְּתוּלֹ֖ת מְעִילִ֑ים וַיֹּצֵ֨א אוֹתָ֤הּ מְשָֽׁרְתוֹ֙ הַח֔וּץ וְנָעַ֥ל הַדֶּ֖לֶת אַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And on her [was] a tunic of passim, for thus were clothed [the] daughters of the king, the virgins, [in] robes; and brought her out his attendant outside and bolted the door after her.

en.L: Now she had on her a tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles], for the virgin daughters of the king were clothed [in] such robes. And his attendant brought her outside and bolted the door after her.
en.B: She was wearing a long-sleeved robe, the kind of robe the king's unmarried daughters wore. His servant put her out and bolted the door behind her.
en.R: Tamar was wearing a special robe with long sleeves. The king's daughters who were not yet married wore robes like that. Amnon's servant put her outside and locked the door behind her.

es.L: Y ella llevaba puesta una túnica [que llegaba hasta las] muñecas [y los tobillos], porque las hijas vírgenes del rey se vestían [con] tales mantos. Y su servidor la sacó afuera y cerró la puerta tras ella con cerrojo.
es.B: Ella llevaba una túnica de mangas largas, como las que vestían las hijas solteras del rey. El criado la sacó afuera y echó el cerrojo a la puerta detrás de ella.
es.R: Tamar llevaba puesta una túnica especial de mangas largas. Las hijas del rey que todavía no se habían casado vestían túnicas así. El criado de Amnón la sacó afuera y cerró la puerta con llave detrás de ella.

fr.L: Or elle avait sur elle une tunique [descendant jusqu’aux] poignets [et aux chevilles], car les filles du roi, les vierges, étaient vêtues de telles robes. Et son serviteur la mit dehors et verrouilla la porte derrière elle.
fr.B: Elle portait une longue robe à manches, la robe que portaient les filles du roi qui n’étaient pas mariées. Le serviteur la mit dehors et verrouilla la porte derrière elle.
fr.R: Tamar portait une robe spéciale à longues manches. Les filles du roi qui n’étaient pas encore mariées portaient des robes comme celle-là. Le serviteur d’Amnon l’a mise dehors et a fermé la porte à clé derrière elle.

vi.L: Nàng mặc một chiếc áo dài [đến] cổ tay [và cổ chân], vì các công chúa còn trinh nữ đều mặc áo choàng như thế. Người hầu của chàng đưa nàng ra ngoài và cài then cửa sau lưng nàng.
vi.B: Nàng đang mặc một chiếc áo dài tay, là loại áo mà các công chúa chưa lấy chồng thường mặc. Người hầu của Am-nôn đưa nàng ra ngoài và cài then cửa lại sau lưng nàng.
vi.R: Ta-ma đang mặc một chiếc áo đặc biệt có tay dài. Các con gái của vua chưa lấy chồng đều mặc áo như thế. Người đầy tớ của Am-nôn đưa nàng ra ngoài và khóa cửa lại sau lưng nàng.

decisions.choice: a tunic of passim: a long robe reaching to the wrists and ankles
decisions.reason: Passim probably means "palms (of the hands) and soles (of the feet)": a full-length robe with long sleeves, as worn by those who did no hard work. It is the same garment Jacob gave Joseph (Genesis 37:3), the only other place it is named. The ancient Greek translation took it to mean a robe reaching the wrists here and "many-colored" in Genesis; the length and sleeves, not the color, seem to be the point.

decisions.choice: the virgin daughters of the king: the robe marked her rank and her state
decisions.reason: The robe showed that she was a king's daughter and unmarried. The narrator pauses to describe it just as she is thrown out, so that the reader sees what has been taken from her; in verse 19 she tears it.

decisions.choice: robes: the outer garments
decisions.reason: The word names a robe or mantle worn over other clothes (1 Samuel 18:4; 24:5). Its place at the end of the clause is awkward in Hebrew, and some suggest it is a slightly changed form of "from long ago" ("so the king's daughters had dressed from of old"). The sense of the verse is not affected.

decisions.choice: a tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles] (Literal); a long-sleeved robe (Balanced); a special robe with long sleeves (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same wording as for Joseph's robe in Genesis 37:3, so that readers can see the link. The familiar "coat of many colors" follows the Greek translation of Genesis.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: The word for the attendant of verse 17 is "one who serves"; Balanced and Readable say "servant". Readable names him as Amnon's servant, since "his" could seem to point to someone else.

decisions.choice: una túnica [que llegaba hasta las] muñecas [y los tobillos] (L); una túnica de mangas largas (B); una túnica especial de mangas largas (R)
decisions.reason: As the English decision (r-en-1), the robe is one reaching to the wrists and ankles, the mark of a king's unmarried daughter; Literal shows the supplied words in brackets.

decisions.choice: su servidor (L); el criado (B, R)
decisions.reason: For this block: the young men and attendants who serve a master (naʿar, meshareth) are 'criados' at Balanced and Readable, and 'jóvenes' or 'servidor' at Literal; 'siervos' is kept for ʿeved, the king's servants, so that the two words stay apart.

decisions.choice: "áo dài [đến] cổ tay [và cổ chân]" (L); "áo dài tay" (B); "áo đặc biệt có tay dài" (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as Joseph's robe in the Vietnamese Genesis 37:3 should be checked by a reviewer so readers see the link; "áo nhiều màu" follows an old guess the meaning decision sets aside.

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֨ח תָּמָ֥ר אֵ֨פֶר֙ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֔הּ וּכְתֹ֧נֶת הַפַּסִּ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יהָ קָרָ֑עָה וַתָּ֤שֶׂם יָדָהּ֙ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֔הּ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ הָל֖וֹךְ וְזָעָֽקָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Tamar ashes on her head, and the tunic of passim which [was] on her she tore, and put her hand on her head and went, going and crying out.

en.L: And Tamar put ashes on her head, and she tore the tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles] that [was] on her, and she put her hand on her head and went away, crying out as she went.
en.B: Tamar put ashes on her head and tore the long-sleeved robe she was wearing. She put her hand on her head and went away, crying aloud as she went.
en.R: Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her special robe with long sleeves. She put her hand on her head to show her grief. Then she went away, crying loudly.

es.L: Y Tamar se echó ceniza sobre la cabeza, y rasgó la túnica [que llegaba hasta las] muñecas [y los tobillos] que [llevaba] puesta, y se puso la mano sobre la cabeza y se fue, gritando mientras andaba.
es.B: Tamar se echó ceniza en la cabeza y rasgó la túnica de mangas largas que llevaba. Se puso la mano sobre la cabeza y se fue, gritando en voz alta mientras caminaba.
es.R: Tamar se echó ceniza en la cabeza y rasgó su túnica especial de mangas largas. Se puso la mano sobre la cabeza para mostrar su dolor. Luego se fue llorando a gritos.

fr.L: Et Tamar mit de la cendre sur sa tête, et la tunique [descendant jusqu’aux] poignets [et aux chevilles] qu’elle avait sur elle, elle la déchira ; et elle mit sa main sur sa tête et s’en alla, poussant des cris en marchant.
fr.B: Tamar répandit de la cendre sur sa tête et déchira la longue robe à manches qu’elle portait. Elle mit la main sur sa tête et s’en alla en criant tout le long du chemin.
fr.R: Tamar a mis de la cendre sur sa tête et a déchiré sa robe spéciale à longues manches. Elle a posé la main sur sa tête pour montrer sa douleur. Puis elle est partie en pleurant très fort.

vi.L: Ta-ma lấy tro rắc lên đầu mình, xé chiếc áo dài [đến] cổ tay [và cổ chân] nàng đang mặc, đặt tay lên đầu và đi, vừa đi vừa kêu khóc.
vi.B: Ta-ma rắc tro lên đầu và xé chiếc áo dài tay mình đang mặc. Nàng đặt tay lên đầu rồi bỏ đi, vừa đi vừa khóc lớn.
vi.R: Ta-ma rắc tro lên đầu và xé chiếc áo đặc biệt có tay dài của mình. Nàng đặt tay lên đầu để tỏ nỗi đau buồn. Rồi nàng bỏ đi, khóc lớn.

decisions.choice: ashes on her head; tore the robe: signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Putting dust or ashes on the head and tearing clothes were the usual signs of grief and disaster (1:2; Joshua 7:6). Tearing the robe that marked her as a king's virgin daughter shows what she has lost.

decisions.choice: put her hand on her head: a gesture of grief and shame
decisions.reason: The same gesture is named in Jeremiah 2:37, of people led away in disgrace.

decisions.choice: went, going and crying out: she cried out as she went, openly
decisions.reason: The verb "go" is doubled, describing an action that went on: she kept crying out as she walked. In the law, a woman's cry for help is what shows that she was forced (Deuteronomy 22:24, 27). Tamar does not hide what has happened.

decisions.choice: to show her grief
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the gesture meant.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֜יהָ אַבְשָׁל֣וֹם אָחִ֗יהָ הַאֲמִינ֣וֹן אָחִיךְ֮ הָיָ֣ה עִמָּךְ֒ וְעַתָּ֞ה אֲחוֹתִ֤י הַחֲרִ֨ישִׁי֙ אָחִ֣יךְ ה֔וּא אַל־תָּשִׁ֥יתִי אֶת־לִבֵּ֖ךְ לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב תָּמָר֙ וְשֹׁ֣מֵמָ֔ה בֵּ֖ית אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם אָחִֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Absalom her brother, [has] Aminon your brother been with you? And now, my sister, be silent; your brother [is] he; do not set your heart to this thing. And dwelt Tamar, and desolate, [in the] house of Absalom her brother.

en.L: And Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now, my sister, keep silent; he [is] your brother. Do not set your heart on this matter." And Tamar dwelt, a desolate [woman], in the house of Absalom her brother.
en.B: Absalom, her brother, asked her, "Has your brother Amnon been with you? Now, my sister, keep quiet. He is your brother. Do not take this matter to heart." So Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, a desolate woman.
en.R: Her brother Absalom asked her, "Has your brother Amnon done this to you? Now, my sister, say nothing about it. He is your brother. Do not let it break your heart." So Tamar lived on in her brother Absalom's house, alone and in despair.

es.L: Y Absalón su hermano le dijo: «¿Ha estado contigo Amnón tu hermano? Pues ahora, hermana mía, guarda silencio; él [es] tu hermano. No pongas tu corazón en este asunto». Y Tamar habitó, desolada, en la casa de Absalón su hermano.
es.B: Absalón, su hermano, le preguntó: «¿Ha estado contigo tu hermano Amnón? Ahora, hermana mía, quédate callada. Es tu hermano. No te tomes esto tan a pecho». Así que Tamar vivió en casa de su hermano Absalón, como una mujer desolada.
es.R: Su hermano Absalón le preguntó: «¿Te hizo esto tu hermano Amnón? Ahora, hermana mía, no digas nada. Él es tu hermano. No dejes que esto te destroce el corazón». Así que Tamar se quedó a vivir en casa de su hermano Absalón, sola y sin esperanza.

fr.L: Et Absalom son frère lui dit : « Amnon ton frère a-t-il été avec toi ? Mais maintenant, ma sœur, tais-toi ; c’[est] ton frère. Ne prends pas cette affaire à cœur. » Et Tamar demeura, désolée, dans la maison d’Absalom son frère.
fr.B: Son frère Absalom lui demanda : « Ton frère Amnon a-t-il été avec toi ? Maintenant, ma sœur, garde le silence. C’est ton frère. Ne prends pas cette affaire à cœur. » Et Tamar vécut, femme désolée, dans la maison de son frère Absalom.
fr.R: Son frère Absalom lui a demandé : « Est-ce que ton frère Amnon t’a fait cela ? Maintenant, ma sœur, n’en parle à personne. C’est ton frère. Ne te laisse pas briser par cette affaire. » Tamar est donc restée dans la maison de son frère Absalom, seule et sans espoir.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm anh nàng nói với nàng: "Có phải Am-nôn anh em đã ở với em không? Nhưng bây giờ, em gái của anh, hãy im lặng; nó [là] anh của em. Đừng để lòng em vào chuyện này." Rồi Ta-ma ở, [một người đàn bà] cô quạnh, trong nhà Áp-sa-lôm anh mình.
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm anh nàng hỏi: "Có phải Am-nôn anh em đã ăn nằm với em không? Bây giờ, em gái của anh, hãy im lặng. Nó là anh của em. Đừng để tâm đến chuyện này." Vậy Ta-ma sống trong nhà Áp-sa-lôm anh mình, như một người đàn bà cô quạnh.
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm anh nàng hỏi: "Am-nôn anh em đã làm chuyện đó với em phải không? Bây giờ, em gái của anh, đừng nói gì với ai cả. Nó là anh của em. Đừng để chuyện này làm tan nát lòng em." Vậy Ta-ma ở lại trong nhà Áp-sa-lôm anh mình, cô đơn và tuyệt vọng.

decisions.choice: been with you: had sexual relations with you
decisions.reason: Absalom guesses at once what has happened and puts it in a restrained way. He asks about "Amnon your brother", setting the deed beside the family bond.

decisions.choice: Aminon: a different form of Amnon's name
decisions.reason: Here alone the Hebrew spells the name Aminon. It may be a scornful little name on Absalom's lips, or just another spelling. It is the same man.

decisions.choice: keep silent; he is your brother; do not set your heart on this: Absalom tells her to bear it quietly
decisions.reason: To "set the heart" on something is to dwell on it or brood over it (verse 33). Absalom's counsel sounds like comfort, but verses 22 and 32 show that he was nursing his own plan in silence.

decisions.choice: desolate: ruined, left alone and without hope of marriage
decisions.reason: The word is used of a land laid waste and of a woman left without husband or children (Isaiah 54:1). Tamar lived on in her brother's house, unmarried and childless, cut off from the life she might have had.

decisions.choice: Amnon
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the usual spelling of the name so that readers are not confused; the meaning decision notes the different Hebrew form.

decisions.choice: done this to you; let it break your heart; alone and in despair
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what Absalom's question means, puts "set your heart on" as letting it break her heart, and explains "desolate" in two simple words.

source.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד שָׁמַ֕ע אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּ֥חַר ל֖וֹ מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And the king David heard all the things the these, and it burned to him greatly.

en.L: And King David heard all these things, and he burned [with anger] greatly.
en.B: When King David heard about all these things, he was very angry.
en.R: When King David heard about all this, he was furious.

es.L: Y el rey David oyó todas estas cosas, y se encendió [en ira] en gran manera.
es.B: Cuando el rey David se enteró de todo esto, se enojó muchísimo.
es.R: Cuando el rey David supo todo lo que había pasado, se puso furioso.

fr.L: Et le roi David apprit toutes ces choses, et il fut très enflammé [de colère].
fr.B: Quand le roi David apprit tout cela, il fut très en colère.
fr.R: Quand le roi David a appris tout cela, il a été furieux.

vi.L: Vua Đa-vít nghe tất cả những việc này, thì [cơn giận] bừng lên rất dữ.
vi.B: Khi vua Đa-vít nghe biết mọi chuyện ấy, vua rất giận.
vi.R: Khi vua Đa-vít nghe biết chuyện này, vua vô cùng tức giận.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text ends with David's anger
alternatives: adds: but he did not trouble his son Amnon, because he loved him, since he was his firstborn (ancient Greek; Qumran)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation, and a Hebrew manuscript of Samuel from Qumran as far as it can be read, add: "but he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, for he was his firstborn." This would explain why David did nothing. The Hebrew text, which does not have the words, is followed here. The longer reading may be original and have dropped out by a copying slip, or may be an early explanation added to the text. Reviewers should check these readings against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: it burned to him: he became angry
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as heat rising in a person, as in 12:5 when David heard Nathan's story.

decisions.choice: very angry, but he does nothing
decisions.reason: The text tells of David's anger but of no punishment for Amnon. Eli was blamed for not restraining his sons (1 Samuel 3:13), and of David's son Adonijah it is later said that his father had never crossed him (1 Kings 1:6). Absalom's silence (verse 22) fills the gap David leaves.

decisions.choice: burned [with anger]
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of burning and brackets "with anger", which the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־דִבֶּ֧ר אַבְשָׁל֛וֹם עִם־אַמְנ֖וֹן לְמֵרָ֣ע וְעַד־ט֑וֹב כִּֽי־שָׂנֵ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶת־אַמְנ֔וֹן עַל־דְּבַר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִנָּ֔ה אֵ֖ת תָּמָ֥ר אֲחֹתֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And not spoke Absalom with Amnon from bad to good, for hated Absalom Amnon over [the] matter that he had humbled Tamar his sister.

en.L: And Absalom did not speak with Amnon, either bad or good, for Absalom hated Amnon on account of his having humbled Tamar his sister.
en.B: Absalom said nothing at all to Amnon, good or bad. He hated Amnon because he had violated his sister Tamar.
en.R: Absalom did not say one word to Amnon, good or bad. He hated Amnon for raping his sister Tamar.

es.L: Y Absalón no habló con Amnón ni malo ni bueno, porque Absalón odiaba a Amnón por haber humillado a Tamar su hermana.
es.B: Absalón no le dijo nada a Amnón, ni bueno ni malo. Lo odiaba porque había deshonrado a su hermana Tamar.
es.R: Absalón no le dirigió ni una sola palabra a Amnón, ni buena ni mala. Lo odiaba por haber violado a su hermana Tamar.

fr.L: Et Absalom ne parla pas avec Amnon, ni en mal ni en bien, car Absalom haïssait Amnon parce qu’il avait humilié Tamar sa sœur.
fr.B: Absalom ne dit plus rien à Amnon, ni en bien ni en mal. Il haïssait Amnon parce qu’il avait fait violence à sa sœur Tamar.
fr.R: Absalom n’a plus dit un seul mot à Amnon, ni en bien ni en mal. Il détestait Amnon parce qu’il avait violé sa sœur Tamar.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm không nói với Am-nôn điều gì, dù xấu hay tốt, vì Áp-sa-lôm ghét Am-nôn về việc nó đã làm nhục Ta-ma em gái mình.
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm không nói với Am-nôn một lời nào, dù tốt hay xấu. Chàng ghét Am-nôn vì Am-nôn đã cưỡng bức Ta-ma em gái mình.
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm không nói với Am-nôn một lời nào, tốt hay xấu cũng không. Chàng ghét Am-nôn vì Am-nôn đã cưỡng hiếp Ta-ma em gái mình.

decisions.choice: from bad to good: nothing at all
decisions.reason: Naming two opposites covers everything between them. Absalom said nothing to Amnon of any kind, as Laban was told to say nothing to Jacob "good or bad" (Genesis 31:24, 29).

decisions.choice: humbled: violated
decisions.reason: The verb of verses 12 and 14.

decisions.choice: he hated Amnon: Absalom's silence hides his hatred
decisions.reason: The verb "hated" is the one used of Amnon's hatred for Tamar in verse 15. Absalom's silence is not peace but a hatred kept hidden, which waits two years (verse 23). "His sister" can be read as Absalom's or Amnon's; she was both.

decisions.choice: violated (Balanced); raping (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verses 12 and 14.
