source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ לִשְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֤וּ גֹֽזְזִים֙ לְאַבְשָׁל֔וֹם בְּבַ֥עַל חָצ֖וֹר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִם־אֶפְרָ֑יִם וַיִּקְרָ֥א אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם לְכָל־בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after two years [of] days, and there were shearers for Absalom in Baal-hazor, which [is] near Ephraim; and invited Absalom all [the] sons of the king.

en.L: And it happened after two full years that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which [is] near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the sons of the king.
en.B: Two full years later, Absalom had sheepshearers at work at Baal-hazor, near Ephraim, and he invited all the king's sons.
en.R: Two whole years later, Absalom's sheep were being sheared at Baal-hazor, near the town of Ephraim. Absalom invited all the king's sons to the celebration.

es.L: Y sucedió, al cabo de dos años completos, que Absalón tenía esquiladores en Baal-hazor, que [está] junto a Efraín, y Absalón invitó a todos los hijos del rey.
es.B: Dos años completos después, Absalón tenía esquiladores trabajando en Baal-hazor, cerca de Efraín, e invitó a todos los hijos del rey.
es.R: Dos años enteros después, estaban esquilando las ovejas de Absalón en Baal-hazor, cerca del pueblo de Efraín. Absalón invitó a la fiesta a todos los hijos del rey.

fr.L: Et il arriva, au bout de deux années entières, qu’Absalom avait des tondeurs à Baal-Hatsor, qui [est] près d’Éphraïm ; et Absalom invita tous les fils du roi.
fr.B: Deux ans plus tard, Absalom faisait tondre ses moutons à Baal-Hatsor, près d’Éphraïm, et il invita tous les fils du roi.
fr.R: Deux années entières plus tard, on tondait les moutons d’Absalom à Baal-Hatsor, près de la ville d’Éphraïm. Absalom a invité tous les fils du roi à la fête.

vi.L: Sau hai năm tròn, Áp-sa-lôm có thợ hớt lông chiên tại Ba-anh Hát-so, gần Ép-ra-im, và Áp-sa-lôm mời tất cả các con trai của vua.
vi.B: Hai năm tròn sau, Áp-sa-lôm có thợ hớt lông chiên làm việc tại Ba-anh Hát-so, gần Ép-ra-im, và chàng mời tất cả các hoàng tử đến.
vi.R: Hai năm sau, người ta hớt lông đàn chiên của Áp-sa-lôm tại Ba-anh Hát-so, gần thành Ép-ra-im. Áp-sa-lôm mời tất cả các con trai của vua đến dự tiệc.

decisions.choice: two years of days: two full years
decisions.reason: Adding "days" to a length of time means the whole of it (Genesis 41:1). Absalom has waited two years in silence since verse 22.

decisions.choice: sheepshearers: the season of shearing, a time of feasting
decisions.reason: Shearing time was a festival for flock owners, with food and wine for the household and guests (1 Samuel 25:2, 8, 36; Genesis 38:12). Absalom's invitation would seem natural.

decisions.choice: Baal-hazor near Ephraim: a place in the hills north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Baal-hazor is usually identified with a high hill about fifteen miles north of Jerusalem. "Ephraim" here is probably a town near it (perhaps the Ephraim of John 11:54), rather than the tribe, whose land lay further north.

decisions.choice: Absalom's sheep were being sheared; to the celebration
decisions.reason: Readable explains "Absalom had sheepshearers" and adds what the invitation was to, from the custom described in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: Baal-Hatsor
decisions.reason: The French transcription of the Hebrew name, with "ts" for the Hebrew sound, as in "Tsiqlag" and "Mitspa" in the Samuel terms note.

decisions.choice: "các hoàng tử" (B) for "the king's sons"
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the usual Vietnamese word for a king's sons; Literal and Readable keep "các con trai của vua", which Readable needs where the father is named.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־נָ֥א גֹזְזִ֖ים לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ יֵֽלֶךְ־נָ֥א הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וַעֲבָדָ֖יו עִם־עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Absalom to the king and said, look please, shearers [are] to your servant; let go please the king and his servants with your servant.

en.L: And Absalom came to the king and said, "Look, please, your servant has sheepshearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant."
en.B: Absalom came to the king and said, "Your servant has sheepshearers at work. Will the king and his officials please come with your servant?"
en.R: Absalom went to the king and said, "Your servant is having his sheep sheared. Please come, my king, and bring your officials with you."

es.L: Y Absalón vino al rey y dijo: «Mira, te ruego, tu siervo tiene esquiladores. Te ruego que vengan el rey y sus siervos con tu siervo».
es.B: Absalón fue a ver al rey y le dijo: «Tu siervo tiene esquiladores trabajando. ¿Querrán el rey y sus oficiales venir con tu siervo?».
es.R: Absalón fue a ver al rey y le dijo: «Tu siervo está esquilando sus ovejas. Por favor, ven, mi rey, y trae contigo a tus oficiales».

fr.L: Et Absalom vint vers le roi et dit : « Voici, je te prie, ton serviteur a des tondeurs ; que le roi, je te prie, vienne avec ses serviteurs, avec ton serviteur. »
fr.B: Absalom alla trouver le roi et lui dit : « Ton serviteur fait tondre ses moutons. Que le roi daigne venir avec ses officiers chez ton serviteur. »
fr.R: Absalom est allé voir le roi et lui a dit : « Ton serviteur fait tondre ses moutons. Viens, s’il te plaît, mon roi, et amène tes officiers avec toi. »

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm đến gặp vua và nói: "Kìa, đầy tớ của vua có thợ hớt lông chiên. Xin vua và các đầy tớ của vua cùng đi với đầy tớ của vua."
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm đến gặp vua và thưa: "Đầy tớ của vua đang có thợ hớt lông chiên. Xin bệ hạ và các quần thần đến dự với đầy tớ của vua."
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm đến gặp vua và thưa: "Con đang cho hớt lông chiên. Xin đức vua đến dự, và xin đem các quần thần theo."

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "I" to the king
decisions.reason: Speaking to a king, a subject referred to himself as "your servant" (9:2; 1 Samuel 20:7-8). Absalom also speaks of David as "the king" rather than "you", as court courtesy required.

decisions.choice: the king and his servants: the king and his court
decisions.reason: "His servants" are David's officials. To invite the king and his whole court was a great honor to offer, and it made the feast seem innocent.

decisions.choice: your servant
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel, the polite "your servant" is kept at every level. Readable keeps it once and then speaks to the king directly.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants here are his court officials, so Balanced and Readable say "officials"; Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: "ton serviteur" (every level); "ses serviteurs" (L), "ses officiers" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note: "your servant" to the king is "ton serviteur" at every level, and the king’s servants are "les serviteurs du roi" at Literal, "les officiers du roi" at Balanced and Readable. Followed through the block.

decisions.choice: tu siervo; sus siervos (L), sus oficiales (B, R)
decisions.reason: For this block, as the terms note: a subject speaking to the king calls himself 'tu siervo' at every level and speaks to him with 'tú'; the king's servants as a body are 'los siervos del rey' at Literal and 'los oficiales del rey' at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "đầy tớ của vua" (L, B) and "con" (R) for Absalom's "your servant"; "vua" (L), "bệ hạ" (B), "đức vua" (R) for the king
decisions.reason: Absalom speaks to his father in court language, which the Samuel terms note renders "đầy tớ của vua" at Literal and Balanced; at Readable a son says "con", since "tôi" would be cold from a son to his father. These forms are kept for subjects addressing the king through this block.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־אַבְשָׁל֗וֹם אַל־בְּנִי֙ אַל־נָ֤א נֵלֵךְ֙ כֻּלָּ֔נוּ וְלֹ֥א נִכְבַּ֖ד עָלֶ֑יךָ וַיִּפְרָץ־בּ֛וֹ וְלֹֽא־אָבָ֥ה לָלֶ֖כֶת וַֽיְבָרֲכֵֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to Absalom, no, my son, let us not go please all of us, and not we will be heavy on you. And he urged him, but not he was willing to go, and he blessed him.

en.L: And the king said to Absalom, "No, my son, let us not all go, so that we will not be heavy on you." And he urged him, but he was not willing to go, and he blessed him.
en.B: "No, my son," the king said to Absalom. "We should not all go; we would only be a burden to you." Absalom pressed him, but he would not go, though he gave him his blessing.
en.R: But the king said to Absalom, "No, my son. We will not all come. It would cost you too much." Absalom kept asking him, but the king still would not go. Instead he gave Absalom his blessing and sent him off.

es.L: Y el rey dijo a Absalón: «No, hijo mío, no vayamos todos, para que no te seamos una carga». Y él le insistió, pero no quiso ir, y lo bendijo.
es.B: «No, hijo mío», le dijo el rey a Absalón. «No debemos ir todos; solo seríamos una carga para ti». Absalón le insistió, pero él no quiso ir, aunque le dio su bendición.
es.R: Pero el rey le dijo a Absalón: «No, hijo mío. No iremos todos. Te costaría demasiado». Absalón le siguió insistiendo, pero el rey no quiso ir. En cambio, le dio su bendición y lo despidió.

fr.L: Et le roi dit à Absalom : « Non, mon fils, n’allons pas tous, afin que nous ne te soyons pas à charge. » Et il le pressa, mais il ne voulut pas aller, et il le bénit.
fr.B: « Non, mon fils, dit le roi à Absalom. Nous n’irons pas tous ; nous ne ferions que te causer de la charge. » Absalom insista, mais le roi ne voulut pas y aller ; il lui donna pourtant sa bénédiction.
fr.R: Mais le roi a répondu à Absalom : « Non, mon fils. Nous ne viendrons pas tous. Cela te coûterait trop cher. » Absalom a insisté encore, mais le roi n’a toujours pas voulu y aller. Il lui a plutôt donné sa bénédiction et l’a laissé partir.

vi.L: Vua nói với Áp-sa-lôm: "Không, con ạ, tất cả chúng ta đừng đi, để chúng ta khỏi làm nặng gánh cho con." Áp-sa-lôm nài ép vua, nhưng vua không muốn đi, và vua chúc phước cho chàng.
vi.B: Vua đáp: "Không được đâu, con ạ. Tất cả chúng ta không nên đi, kẻo thành gánh nặng cho con." Áp-sa-lôm nài nỉ mãi, nhưng vua vẫn không chịu đi, chỉ chúc phước cho chàng.
vi.R: Nhưng vua nói với Áp-sa-lôm: "Không được, con ạ. Chúng ta không đi hết được đâu. Con sẽ tốn kém quá." Áp-sa-lôm cứ nài nỉ, nhưng vua vẫn không chịu đi. Vua chúc phước cho Áp-sa-lôm và cho chàng về.

decisions.choice: be heavy on you: be a burden, a cost to you
decisions.reason: To feed and lodge the king and his whole court would have cost a great deal. David refuses kindly, out of concern for his son.

decisions.choice: urged him: pressed him hard
decisions.reason: The verb means to break through. Here it describes insistent pleading; it returns in verse 27.

decisions.choice: blessed him: gave him his good wishes as he left
decisions.reason: A blessing was often given when someone took leave (Genesis 47:10; 2 Samuel 19:40). David sends Absalom off with his goodwill, unaware of what is planned.

decisions.choice: It would cost you too much; and sent him off
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "be heavy on you" means and adds that the blessing was a farewell, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם וָלֹ֕א יֵֽלֶךְ־נָ֥א אִתָּ֖נוּ אַמְנ֣וֹן אָחִ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָ֥מָּה יֵלֵ֖ךְ עִמָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Absalom, and if not, let go please with us Amnon my brother. And said to him the king, why should he go with you?

en.L: And Absalom said, "If not, please let Amnon my brother go with us." And the king said to him, "Why should he go with you?"
en.B: Then Absalom said, "If you will not come, then please let my brother Amnon go with us." The king asked him, "Why should he go with you?"
en.R: Then Absalom said, "If you will not come, please let my brother Amnon come with us." The king asked, "Why should he go with you?"

es.L: Y Absalón dijo: «Si no, te ruego que venga con nosotros Amnón mi hermano». Y el rey le dijo: «¿Para qué ha de ir contigo?».
es.B: Entonces Absalón dijo: «Si tú no vienes, deja por lo menos que mi hermano Amnón venga con nosotros». El rey le preguntó: «¿Por qué ha de ir contigo?».
es.R: Entonces Absalón dijo: «Si tú no vienes, por favor deja que mi hermano Amnón venga con nosotros». El rey le preguntó: «¿Por qué tiene que ir contigo?».

fr.L: Et Absalom dit : « Sinon, que vienne avec nous, je te prie, Amnon mon frère. » Et le roi lui dit : « Pourquoi irait-il avec toi ? »
fr.B: Absalom reprit : « Si tu ne viens pas, permets du moins à mon frère Amnon de venir avec nous. » Le roi lui demanda : « Pourquoi irait-il avec toi ? »
fr.R: Alors Absalom a dit : « Si tu ne viens pas, laisse au moins mon frère Amnon venir avec nous. » Le roi a demandé : « Pourquoi irait-il avec toi ? »

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm nói: "Nếu không, xin để Am-nôn anh con đi với chúng con." Vua nói với chàng: "Sao nó phải đi với con?"
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm thưa: "Nếu cha không đến, thì xin cho Am-nôn anh con đi với chúng con." Vua hỏi: "Sao nó lại phải đi với con?"
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm thưa: "Nếu cha không đến, xin cho anh Am-nôn của con đi với chúng con." Vua hỏi: "Sao nó phải đi với con?"

decisions.choice: and if not: if you will not come
decisions.reason: The short words mean "if you will not go yourself". Absalom has been aiming at this request all along.

decisions.choice: Amnon my brother: the king's firstborn, as the king's stand-in
decisions.reason: Amnon was David's eldest son and heir (3:2). If the king would not come, it would seem fitting for his firstborn to come in his place. Absalom calls him "my brother" while planning his death.

decisions.choice: why should he go with you: the king hesitates
decisions.reason: The question may show that David sensed something wrong, or only that he saw no need. The text does not say, but he gives way in verse 27.

decisions.choice: If you will not come
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the bare "if not".

source.text: וַיִּפְרָץ־בּ֖וֹ אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אִתּוֹ֙ אֶת־אַמְנ֔וֹן וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And urged him Absalom, and he sent with him Amnon and all [the] sons of the king.

en.L: And Absalom urged him, and he sent Amnon and all the sons of the king with him.
en.B: But Absalom kept pressing him, so he let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.
en.R: But Absalom kept on asking, so the king let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom.

es.L: Y Absalón le insistió, y envió con él a Amnón y a todos los hijos del rey.
es.B: Pero Absalón siguió insistiendo, así que dejó que Amnón y todos los hijos del rey fueran con él.
es.R: Pero Absalón siguió insistiendo, así que el rey dejó que Amnón y todos sus otros hijos fueran con Absalón.

fr.L: Et Absalom le pressa, et il envoya avec lui Amnon et tous les fils du roi.
fr.B: Mais Absalom insista tant que le roi laissa partir avec lui Amnon et tous les fils du roi.
fr.R: Mais Absalom a continué à insister, et le roi a laissé Amnon et tous ses autres fils partir avec Absalom.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm nài ép vua, và vua cho Am-nôn cùng tất cả các con trai của vua đi với chàng.
vi.B: Nhưng Áp-sa-lôm cứ nài nỉ mãi, nên vua cho Am-nôn và tất cả các hoàng tử đi với chàng.
vi.R: Nhưng Áp-sa-lôm cứ nài nỉ mãi, nên vua cho Am-nôn và tất cả các con trai khác của mình đi với Áp-sa-lôm.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text ends with the sending of the king's sons
alternatives: adds: And Absalom made a feast like a king's feast (ancient Greek; Qumran)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation, supported by a Hebrew manuscript from Qumran, adds: "And Absalom made a feast like the feast of a king." The added words fit the story and recall Nabal's feast at shearing time (1 Samuel 25:36), but the Hebrew text is followed here. Reviewers should check the readings.

decisions.choice: urged him: as in verse 25
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 25. This time the king gives way.

decisions.choice: all his other sons
decisions.reason: Readable says "other" because Amnon has just been named, and names Absalom where "him" could be unclear.

source.text: וַיְצַו֩ אַבְשָׁל֨וֹם אֶת־נְעָרָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר רְא֣וּ נָ֠א כְּט֨וֹב לֵב־אַמְנ֤וֹן בַּיַּ֨יִן֙ וְאָמַרְתִּ֣י אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם הַכּ֧וּ אֶת־אַמְנ֛וֹן וַהֲמִתֶּ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ אַל־תִּירָ֑אוּ הֲל֗וֹא כִּ֤י אָֽנֹכִי֙ צִוִּ֣יתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם חִזְק֖וּ וִהְי֥וּ לִבְנֵי־חָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded Absalom his young men, saying, see please, when [is] good [the] heart of Amnon with wine, and I say to you, strike Amnon, and you will kill him; do not fear; [is it] not that I, I have commanded you? Be strong and be sons of valor.

en.L: And Absalom commanded his young men, saying, "See now: when Amnon's heart is merry with wine, and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon,' then kill him. Do not be afraid. Have not I myself commanded you? Be strong and be sons of valor."
en.B: Absalom gave his servants these orders: "Watch closely. When Amnon is in high spirits from the wine and I tell you, 'Strike Amnon,' then kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not given you the order myself? Be strong and act like brave men."
en.R: Absalom gave orders to his servants. "Listen," he said. "Wait until Amnon has drunk a lot of wine and is feeling happy. Then I will say to you, 'Kill Amnon!' When I do, kill him. Do not be afraid. I am the one giving you the order. Be strong and brave!"

es.L: Y Absalón dio órdenes a sus jóvenes, diciendo: «Miren ahora: cuando el corazón de Amnón esté alegre por el vino, y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} diga: “{{plural_you:Hieran|Herid}} a Amnón”, {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. ¿No soy yo quien {{plural_you:les|os}} lo ha mandado? {{plural_you:Esfuércense|Esforzaos}} y {{plural_you:sean|sed}} hombres valientes».
es.B: Absalón dio estas órdenes a sus criados: «{{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} atentos. Cuando Amnón esté alegre por el vino y yo {{plural_you:les|os}} diga: “{{plural_you:Hieran|Herid}} a Amnón”, {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. ¿Acaso no soy yo mismo quien {{plural_you:les|os}} da la orden? {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fuertes y {{plural_you:pórtense|portaos}} como valientes».
es.R: Absalón dio órdenes a sus criados. «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}», les dijo. «{{plural_you:Esperen|Esperad}} hasta que Amnón haya bebido mucho vino y esté contento. Entonces yo {{plural_you:les|os}} diré: “¡{{plural_you:Maten|Matad}} a Amnón!”. Cuando lo diga, {{plural_you:mátenlo|matadlo}}. No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. Yo soy el que {{plural_you:les|os}} da la orden. ¡{{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} fuertes y valientes!».

fr.L: Et Absalom commanda à ses jeunes gens, disant : « Voyez donc : quand le cœur d’Amnon sera joyeux par le vin et que je vous dirai : “Frappez Amnon”, alors tuez-le. Ne craignez pas. N’est-ce pas moi qui vous l’ai commandé ? Soyez forts et soyez des fils de vaillance. »
fr.B: Absalom donna cet ordre à ses serviteurs : « Faites bien attention. Quand Amnon sera gai sous l’effet du vin et que je vous dirai : “Frappez Amnon”, tuez-le. N’ayez pas peur. N’est-ce pas moi qui vous en donne l’ordre ? Soyez forts et montrez-vous vaillants. »
fr.R: Absalom a donné des ordres à ses serviteurs. Il leur a dit : « Écoutez. Attendez qu’Amnon ait bu beaucoup de vin et qu’il soit joyeux. Alors je vous dirai : “Tuez Amnon !” À ce moment-là, tuez-le. N’ayez pas peur. C’est moi qui vous en donne l’ordre. Soyez forts et courageux ! »

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm truyền lệnh cho các đầy tớ trẻ của mình rằng: "Hãy coi chừng: khi lòng Am-nôn vui vì rượu, và ta nói với các ngươi: 'Hãy đánh Am-nôn,' thì hãy giết nó. Đừng sợ. Chẳng phải chính ta đã ra lệnh cho các ngươi sao? Hãy mạnh mẽ và làm những người dũng cảm."
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm ra lệnh cho các đầy tớ mình: "Hãy để ý. Khi Am-nôn đã ngà ngà say rượu mà ta bảo các ngươi: 'Đánh Am-nôn,' thì hãy giết nó. Đừng sợ. Chẳng phải chính ta đã ra lệnh cho các ngươi sao? Hãy mạnh mẽ và hành động như những người can đảm."
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm ra lệnh cho các đầy tớ mình: "Nghe đây. Hãy đợi đến khi Am-nôn uống nhiều rượu và đang vui vẻ. Lúc ấy ta sẽ bảo các ngươi: 'Giết Am-nôn!' Khi ta nói thế, hãy giết nó. Đừng sợ. Chính ta là người ra lệnh cho các ngươi. Hãy mạnh mẽ và can đảm lên!"

decisions.choice: when Amnon's heart is good with wine: when he is merry and drunk
decisions.reason: A "good heart" with wine means being cheerful from drinking (1 Samuel 25:36, of Nabal at his shearing feast; Esther 1:10). Amnon would be off his guard.

decisions.choice: have not I myself commanded you: the responsibility is mine
decisions.reason: "I" is stressed in the Hebrew. Absalom takes the guilt on himself, so his men need not fear to strike the king's son.

decisions.choice: be sons of valor: be brave men
decisions.reason: A "son of" a quality is someone who has it. "Sons of valor" are men who are brave and able to fight (1 Samuel 18:17).

decisions.choice: his young men: his servants
decisions.reason: The word means young men, and often young men in someone's service. Here they are Absalom's own men, whom he can command (verse 29).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "young men"; Balanced and Readable say "servants", their place here.

decisions.choice: has drunk a lot of wine and is feeling happy; Kill Amnon
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom and puts the order "strike" as "kill", which is what Absalom means, as the next words show.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} forms for Absalom's orders to his men
decisions.reason: Absalom speaks to a group, so every plural 'you', including the order he will give them ('Hieran a Amnón'), takes the plural_you setting, as in the Pentateuch.

source.text: וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֞וּ נַעֲרֵ֤י אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ לְאַמְנ֔וֹן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ׀כָּל־בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַֽיִּרְכְּב֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ עַל־פִּרְדּ֖וֹ וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And did [the] young men of Absalom to Amnon just as had commanded Absalom; and arose all [the] sons of the king and rode each on his mule and fled.

en.L: And the young men of Absalom did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded. And all the sons of the king rose up, and each mounted his mule, and they fled.
en.B: So Absalom's servants did to Amnon exactly what Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's sons got up, mounted their mules and fled.
en.R: So Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's other sons jumped up, got on their mules and rode away as fast as they could.

es.L: Y los jóvenes de Absalón hicieron con Amnón tal como Absalón había mandado. Y todos los hijos del rey se levantaron, y montó cada uno en su mula, y huyeron.
es.B: Así que los criados de Absalón hicieron con Amnón exactamente lo que Absalón había ordenado. Entonces todos los hijos del rey se levantaron, montaron en sus mulas y huyeron.
es.R: Así que los criados de Absalón mataron a Amnón, tal como Absalón les había ordenado. Entonces todos los otros hijos del rey se levantaron de un salto, se subieron a sus mulas y huyeron a toda prisa.

fr.L: Et les jeunes gens d’Absalom firent à Amnon comme Absalom l’avait commandé. Et tous les fils du roi se levèrent, et ils montèrent chacun sur son mulet et s’enfuirent.
fr.B: Les serviteurs d’Absalom traitèrent Amnon comme Absalom l’avait ordonné. Alors tous les fils du roi se levèrent, montèrent sur leurs mulets et s’enfuirent.
fr.R: Les serviteurs d’Absalom ont donc tué Amnon, comme Absalom l’avait ordonné. Alors tous les autres fils du roi se sont levés d’un bond. Ils sont montés sur leurs mulets et se sont enfuis aussi vite qu’ils pouvaient.

vi.L: Các đầy tớ trẻ của Áp-sa-lôm làm cho Am-nôn đúng như Áp-sa-lôm đã truyền. Tất cả các con trai của vua đứng dậy, mỗi người cưỡi con la của mình mà chạy trốn.
vi.B: Vậy các đầy tớ của Áp-sa-lôm làm cho Am-nôn đúng như lệnh Áp-sa-lôm. Bấy giờ tất cả các hoàng tử đứng dậy, ai nấy leo lên lưng la của mình mà chạy trốn.
vi.R: Vậy các đầy tớ của Áp-sa-lôm giết Am-nôn đúng như Áp-sa-lôm đã ra lệnh. Tất cả các con trai khác của vua vội đứng dậy, leo lên lưng la và phóng đi thật nhanh.

decisions.choice: did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded: they killed him
decisions.reason: The narrator does not describe the killing; the order in verse 28 has already said what was to be done.

decisions.choice: mule: the mount of the royal family
decisions.reason: Mules were costly animals ridden by the king's household (18:9; 1 Kings 1:33, 38). Each son rode his own.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: As in verse 28.

decisions.choice: killed Amnon; other sons; as fast as they could
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the servants did, makes clear that Amnon is not among those who fled, and brings out the haste in "fled".

source.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ הֵ֣מָּה בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהַשְּׁמֻעָ֣ה בָ֔אָה אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הִכָּ֤ה אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֶת־כָּל־בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹֽא־נוֹתַ֥ר מֵהֶ֖ם אֶחָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was, they [were] on the way, and the report came to David, saying, struck Absalom all [the] sons of the king, and not is left of them one.

en.L: And while they [were] on the way, the report came to David, saying, "Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king, and not one of them is left."
en.B: While they were still on the road, the report reached David: "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons; not one of them is left!"
en.R: While they were still on their way, news reached David: "Absalom has killed all the king's sons! Not one of them is left alive!"

es.L: Y estando ellos [aún] en el camino, llegó a David la noticia, diciendo: «Absalón ha matado a todos los hijos del rey, y no ha quedado ni uno de ellos».
es.B: Mientras todavía estaban en el camino, le llegó a David la noticia: «¡Absalón ha matado a todos los hijos del rey; no ha quedado ni uno!».
es.R: Mientras ellos todavía iban de camino, le llegó a David la noticia: «¡Absalón ha matado a todos los hijos del rey! ¡No ha quedado ni uno con vida!».

fr.L: Et pendant qu’ils [étaient] en chemin, la rumeur parvint à David, disant : « Absalom a frappé tous les fils du roi, et il n’en reste pas un seul. »
fr.B: Ils étaient encore en chemin quand la nouvelle parvint à David : « Absalom a abattu tous les fils du roi ; il n’en reste pas un seul ! »
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils étaient encore en route, une nouvelle est arrivée jusqu’à David : « Absalom a tué tous les fils du roi ! Il n’en reste pas un seul en vie ! »

vi.L: Trong khi họ [còn] đang đi đường, thì tin đến tai Đa-vít rằng: "Áp-sa-lôm đã đánh giết tất cả các con trai của vua, không còn sót lại một ai."
vi.B: Họ còn đang trên đường thì có tin báo đến Đa-vít: "Áp-sa-lôm đã giết hết các hoàng tử, không còn sót một người nào!"
vi.R: Trong khi họ còn đang trên đường về, có tin báo đến Đa-vít: "Áp-sa-lôm đã giết hết các con trai của vua! Không một người nào còn sống!"

decisions.choice: the report: news passed on by word of mouth
decisions.reason: The word means something heard. It ran ahead of the king's sons and, as rumors do, made the disaster greater than it was.

decisions.choice: while they were on the way: the rumor arrives first
decisions.reason: The king's sons fleeing on mules took some time to reach Jerusalem, and the rumor outran them.

decisions.choice: left alive
decisions.reason: Readable adds "alive" to make the sense of "left" plain.

source.text: וַיָּ֧קָם הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וַיִּקְרַ֥ע אֶת־בְּגָדָ֖יו וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב אָ֑רְצָה וְכָל־עֲבָדָ֥יו נִצָּבִ֖ים קְרֻעֵ֥י בְגָדִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And arose the king and tore his garments and lay [on the] ground, and all his servants [were] standing, torn of garments.

en.L: And the king rose and tore his garments and lay on the ground, and all his servants [were] standing [by with their] garments torn.
en.B: The king rose, tore his clothes and lay on the ground. All his officials stood beside him with their clothes torn.
en.R: The king stood up and tore his clothes in grief. Then he lay down on the ground. All his officials stood beside him, and they had torn their clothes too.

es.L: Y el rey se levantó y rasgó sus vestidos y se tendió en tierra, y todos sus siervos [estaban] de pie [con sus] vestidos rasgados.
es.B: El rey se levantó, se rasgó la ropa y se tendió en el suelo. Todos sus oficiales estaban de pie a su lado con la ropa rasgada.
es.R: El rey se levantó y se rasgó la ropa en señal de dolor. Luego se tendió en el suelo. Todos sus oficiales estaban de pie a su lado, y también ellos se habían rasgado la ropa.

fr.L: Et le roi se leva, et déchira ses vêtements, et se coucha par terre ; et tous ses serviteurs [se tenaient là, les] vêtements déchirés.
fr.B: Le roi se leva, déchira ses vêtements et se coucha par terre. Tous ses officiers se tenaient près de lui, les vêtements déchirés.
fr.R: Le roi s’est levé et a déchiré ses vêtements de chagrin. Puis il s’est couché par terre. Tous ses officiers se tenaient près de lui, et ils avaient eux aussi déchiré leurs vêtements.

vi.L: Vua đứng dậy, xé áo mình và nằm xuống đất; tất cả các đầy tớ vua đứng [bên cạnh với] áo xé rách.
vi.B: Vua đứng dậy, xé áo mình và nằm xuống đất. Tất cả các quần thần đều đứng bên cạnh, áo xé rách.
vi.R: Vua đứng dậy và xé áo mình vì đau buồn. Rồi vua nằm xuống đất. Tất cả các quần thần đứng bên cạnh vua, và họ cũng xé áo mình.

decisions.choice: tore his garments and lay on the ground: the signs of deepest mourning
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes and lying on the ground showed grief and helplessness (1:11; 12:16). The officials join their king in mourning.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials, as in verse 24.

decisions.choice: in grief
decisions.reason: Readable gives the reason for the custom.

decisions.choice: "các đầy tớ vua" (L); "các quần thần" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for the king's servants who are his officials; kept through this block.

source.text: וַיַּ֡עַן יוֹנָדָ֣ב׀בֶּן־שִׁמְעָ֨ה אֲחִֽי־דָוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־יֹאמַ֤ר אֲדֹנִי֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַנְּעָרִ֤ים בְּנֵֽי־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הֵמִ֔יתוּ כִּֽי־אַמְנ֥וֹן לְבַדּ֖וֹ מֵ֑ת כִּֽי־עַל־פִּ֤י אַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ הָיְתָ֣ה שׂוּמָ֔ה מִיּוֹם֙ עַנֹּת֔וֹ אֵ֖ת תָּמָ֥ר אֲחֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Jonadab son of Shimeah, brother of David, and said, let not say my lord, all the young men, the sons of the king, they have killed, for Amnon alone has died; for on [the] mouth of Absalom it has been set from [the] day of his humbling Tamar his sister.

en.L: And Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David's brother, answered and said, "Let not my lord say [that] they have killed all the young men, the sons of the king, for Amnon alone is dead. For by the mouth of Absalom this has been set from the day that he humbled Tamar his sister.
en.B: But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, spoke up: "My lord should not think they have killed all the young men, the king's sons. Only Amnon is dead. Absalom has been determined to do this ever since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
en.R: But Jonadab spoke up. He was the son of David's brother Shimeah. "My lord, do not think that all the young princes have been killed. Only Amnon is dead. Absalom has been planning this ever since the day Amnon raped his sister Tamar.

es.L: Y Jonadab hijo de Simea, hermano de David, respondió y dijo: «No diga mi señor [que] han matado a todos los jóvenes, los hijos del rey, porque solo Amnón ha muerto. Porque por boca de Absalón esto estaba decidido desde el día en que humilló a Tamar su hermana.
es.B: Pero Jonadab hijo de Simea, hermano de David, intervino: «Mi señor no debe pensar que han matado a todos los jóvenes, los hijos del rey. Solo Amnón ha muerto. Absalón estaba decidido a hacer esto desde el día en que Amnón deshonró a su hermana Tamar.
es.R: Pero Jonadab intervino. Era hijo de Simea, el hermano de David. «Mi señor, no pienses que han matado a todos los jóvenes príncipes. Solo Amnón ha muerto. Absalón lo venía planeando desde el día en que Amnón violó a su hermana Tamar.

fr.L: Et Jonadab, fils de Shiméa, frère de David, répondit et dit : « Que mon seigneur ne dise pas qu’ils ont tué tous les jeunes gens, les fils du roi, car Amnon seul est mort. Car sur la bouche d’Absalom cela était fixé depuis le jour où il humilia Tamar sa sœur.
fr.B: Mais Jonadab, fils de Shiméa, le frère de David, prit la parole : « Que mon seigneur ne pense pas qu’on a tué tous les jeunes gens, les fils du roi. Seul Amnon est mort. Absalom y était résolu depuis le jour où Amnon a fait violence à sa sœur Tamar.
fr.R: Mais Jonadab a pris la parole. C’était le fils de Shiméa, le frère de David. « Mon seigneur, ne crois pas que tous les jeunes princes ont été tués. Seul Amnon est mort. Absalom préparait cela depuis le jour où Amnon a violé sa sœur Tamar.

vi.L: Giô-na-đáp con trai Si-mê-a, anh của Đa-vít, lên tiếng nói: "Xin chúa tôi đừng nói [rằng] họ đã giết tất cả các thanh niên, là các con trai của vua, vì chỉ một mình Am-nôn chết thôi. Vì theo miệng Áp-sa-lôm, điều này đã được định từ ngày nó làm nhục Ta-ma em gái mình.
vi.B: Nhưng Giô-na-đáp con trai Si-mê-a, anh của Đa-vít, lên tiếng: "Xin bệ hạ đừng nghĩ rằng họ đã giết hết các hoàng tử. Chỉ có Am-nôn chết thôi. Áp-sa-lôm đã quyết làm việc này từ ngày Am-nôn cưỡng bức Ta-ma em gái mình.
vi.R: Nhưng Giô-na-đáp lên tiếng. Anh ta là con trai Si-mê-a, anh của Đa-vít. "Thưa đức vua, xin đừng nghĩ rằng các hoàng tử đều đã bị giết. Chỉ có Am-nôn chết thôi. Áp-sa-lôm đã tính chuyện này từ ngày Am-nôn cưỡng hiếp Ta-ma em gái mình.

decisions.choice: on the mouth of Absalom it has been set: Absalom has been resolved on this
alternatives: by Absalom's command it was decided
it could be seen on Absalom's face
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. It may mean that the killing was settled by Absalom's own word ("mouth" as in a command), or that it was written on his face, as if his look had shown it since that day. Either way Jonadab says that Absalom had meant to do this for two years.

decisions.choice: let not my lord say: my lord should not think
decisions.reason: "Say" here means to say to oneself, to think or suppose.

decisions.choice: Jonadab: the man who planned Amnon's trick
decisions.reason: The "shrewd" friend of verses 3-5 now knows the mind of the other side as well. He who gave Amnon the plan that led to this speaks calmly to the grieving king.

decisions.choice: his humbling Tamar: Amnon's rape of Tamar
decisions.reason: The verb of verses 12, 14 and 22.

decisions.choice: Absalom has been determined to do this (Balanced); Absalom has been planning this (Readable); violated / raped
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom without choosing between its two pictures. They name Amnon where the Hebrew says "he", and say "violated" and "raped" as in verses 12-22. Readable puts "the young men, the sons of the king" as "the young princes".

decisions.choice: "mon seigneur"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note, a subject calls the king "mon seigneur" and "mon seigneur le roi" at every level; Readable keeps "mon seigneur" where the English Readable says "My lord", and says "mon roi" where it says "my king".

decisions.choice: "chúa tôi" (L); "bệ hạ" (B); "đức vua" (R) for "my lord" said to the king
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for "my lord the king"; Jonadab, the king's nephew, uses the court forms, and they are kept through this block.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה אַל־יָשֵׂם֩ אֲדֹנִ֨י הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֶל־לִבּוֹ֙ דָּבָ֣ר לֵאמֹ֔ר כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מֵ֑תוּ כִּֽי־אִם־אַמְנ֥וֹן לְבַדּ֖וֹ מֵֽת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And now let not set my lord the king to his heart a word, saying, all [the] sons of the king have died; for only Amnon alone has died.

en.L: And now let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, saying, 'All the sons of the king are dead,' for only Amnon alone is dead."
en.B: So now, my lord the king should not take to heart the report that all the king's sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead."
en.R: So, my king, do not believe the news that all your sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead."

es.L: Y ahora, no tome a pecho mi señor el rey la cosa, diciendo: “Todos los hijos del rey han muerto”, porque solo Amnón ha muerto».
es.B: Así que ahora, mi señor el rey no debe tomar a pecho la noticia de que todos los hijos del rey han muerto. Solo Amnón ha muerto».
es.R: Así que, mi rey, no creas la noticia de que todos tus hijos han muerto. Solo Amnón ha muerto».

fr.L: Et maintenant, que mon seigneur le roi ne prenne pas la chose à cœur, disant : “Tous les fils du roi sont morts”, car Amnon seul est mort. »
fr.B: Que mon seigneur le roi ne prenne donc pas à cœur la nouvelle que tous les fils du roi sont morts. Seul Amnon est mort. »
fr.R: Alors, mon roi, ne crois pas la nouvelle qui dit que tous tes fils sont morts. Seul Amnon est mort. »

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, xin chúa tôi là vua đừng để lòng điều này mà nói rằng: 'Tất cả các con trai của vua đều đã chết,' vì chỉ một mình Am-nôn chết thôi."
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, xin bệ hạ đừng để tâm đến tin đồn rằng tất cả các hoàng tử đã chết. Chỉ có Am-nôn chết mà thôi."
vi.R: Vậy xin đức vua đừng tin tin đồn rằng tất cả các con trai của vua đã chết. Chỉ có Am-nôn chết thôi."

decisions.choice: set to his heart: take seriously, be troubled by
decisions.reason: To set something to the heart is to dwell on it and let it weigh on one (verse 20). Jonadab tells the king not to believe the rumor.

decisions.choice: only Amnon alone: the point is repeated
decisions.reason: Jonadab says it a second time (verse 32), with two words for "only", to calm the king.

decisions.choice: do not believe the news
decisions.reason: Readable puts the idiom "set to his heart" as not believing the report, which is its sense here.

decisions.choice: mi señor el rey (L, B); mi rey (R)
decisions.reason: For this block, as the terms note: 'mi señor el rey' at Literal and Balanced, with the king addressed in the third person where the Hebrew does so; Readable says 'mi rey' and 'tú', as the English Readable says 'my king'.

source.text: וַיִּבְרַ֖ח אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם וַיִּשָּׂ֞א הַנַּ֤עַר הַצֹּפֶה֙ אֶת־עֵינָ֔יו וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֨ה עַם־רַ֜ב הֹלְכִ֥ים מִדֶּ֛רֶךְ אַחֲרָ֖יו מִצַּ֥ד הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And fled Absalom. And lifted the young man, the watchman, his eyes and saw, and look, many people [were] coming from [the] road behind him from [the] side of the mountain.

en.L: And Absalom fled. And the young man who was keeping watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and look, many people [were] coming from the road behind him, from the side of the hill.
en.B: Meanwhile Absalom fled. The young man on watch looked up and saw many people coming along the road behind him, down the side of the hill.
en.R: Meanwhile, Absalom ran away. The young man on guard looked out and saw a large crowd coming down the hillside on the road behind him.

es.L: Y Absalón huyó. Y el joven que estaba de guardia alzó sus ojos y miró, y he aquí, mucha gente venía por el camino detrás de él, por la ladera del monte.
es.B: Mientras tanto, Absalón huyó. El joven que estaba de guardia levantó la vista y vio a mucha gente que venía por el camino detrás de él, bajando por la ladera del monte.
es.R: Mientras tanto, Absalón huyó. El joven que hacía guardia miró y vio a una gran multitud que bajaba por la ladera del monte, por el camino que estaba detrás de él.

fr.L: Et Absalom s’enfuit. Et le jeune homme qui faisait le guet leva les yeux et regarda, et voici, beaucoup de gens venaient par le chemin derrière lui, du côté de la colline.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, Absalom s’enfuit. Le jeune homme qui faisait le guet leva les yeux et vit une foule nombreuse qui arrivait par le chemin derrière lui, au flanc de la colline.
fr.R: Pendant ce temps, Absalom s’est enfui. Le jeune homme qui montait la garde a regardé au loin. Il a vu une grande foule qui descendait la colline par le chemin derrière lui.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm chạy trốn. Người thanh niên canh gác ngước mắt lên nhìn, và kìa, nhiều người đang đi đến từ con đường phía sau anh ta, từ sườn đồi.
vi.B: Trong khi đó Áp-sa-lôm đã chạy trốn. Người thanh niên đứng canh ngước nhìn lên, thấy rất đông người đang theo con đường phía sau mình đi xuống sườn đồi.
vi.R: Trong lúc đó Áp-sa-lôm đã chạy trốn. Người thanh niên canh gác nhìn ra và thấy một đám đông đang đi xuống sườn đồi theo con đường phía sau mình.

decisions.choice: Absalom fled: a brief aside
decisions.reason: The narrator breaks off to say what Absalom did while the king mourned. The same words return in verses 37 and 38.

decisions.choice: the road behind him: a road coming from behind the watchman
alternatives: from the road to the west
from the road of Horonaim (ancient Greek)
decisions.reason: "Behind" may simply mean behind the watchman as he faced out, or it may mean "west", since the Hebrew way of giving directions faced east, with the west behind. The ancient Greek translation reads "the road of Horonaim" and adds the watchman's report to the king; it may reflect a fuller Hebrew text. The Hebrew is followed here; reviewers should check the Greek.

decisions.choice: the young man keeping watch: a lookout on the city wall
decisions.reason: A watchman stood on the wall or gate tower to report anyone approaching the city (18:24-27).

decisions.choice: looked up (Balanced); looked out (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Lifted up his eyes" is the Hebrew way of saying someone looked. Balanced and Readable leave out the second "look", which only draws attention to the sight.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יֽוֹנָדָב֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הִנֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בָּ֑אוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר עַבְדְּךָ֖ כֵּ֥ן הָיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jonadab to the king, look, [the] sons of the king have come; according to [the] word of your servant, so it has happened.

en.L: And Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the sons of the king have come! As your servant said, so it has happened."
en.B: Jonadab said to the king, "See, the king's sons are here! It has happened just as your servant said."
en.R: Jonadab said to the king, "Look, your sons are coming! It is just as I, your servant, told you."

es.L: Y Jonadab dijo al rey: «¡Mira, los hijos del rey han venido! Conforme a la palabra de tu siervo, así ha sucedido».
es.B: Jonadab le dijo al rey: «¡Mira, ya están aquí los hijos del rey! Ha sucedido tal como dijo tu siervo».
es.R: Jonadab le dijo al rey: «¡Mira, ya vienen tus hijos! Es tal como yo, tu siervo, te dije».

fr.L: Et Jonadab dit au roi : « Voici, les fils du roi sont arrivés ! Selon la parole de ton serviteur, ainsi il en est. »
fr.B: Jonadab dit au roi : « Vois, les fils du roi arrivent ! Tout s’est passé comme ton serviteur l’avait dit. »
fr.R: Jonadab a dit au roi : « Regarde, tes fils arrivent ! C’est bien comme moi, ton serviteur, je te l’avais dit. »

vi.L: Giô-na-đáp nói với vua: "Kìa, các con trai của vua đã đến! Như lời đầy tớ của vua đã nói, việc đã xảy ra như vậy."
vi.B: Giô-na-đáp tâu với vua: "Kìa, các hoàng tử đã về! Mọi việc đúng như đầy tớ của vua đã nói."
vi.R: Giô-na-đáp nói với vua: "Kìa, các con trai của đức vua đang về! Đúng như tôi đã thưa với đức vua."

decisions.choice: your servant: Jonadab speaks of himself politely
decisions.reason: As in verse 24, a subject speaking to the king calls himself "your servant". Jonadab claims credit for being right.

decisions.choice: your servant
decisions.reason: Kept at every level, as in verse 24; Readable adds "I" so the reader sees that Jonadab means himself.

decisions.choice: your sons
decisions.reason: Readable says "your sons", since Jonadab is speaking to their father.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀כְּכַלֹּת֣וֹ לְדַבֵּ֗ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה בְנֵֽי־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ בָּ֔אוּ וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ וְגַם־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְכָל־עֲבָדָ֔יו בָּכ֕וּ בְּכִ֖י גָּד֥וֹל מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as he finished speaking, and look, [the] sons of the king came and lifted up their voice and wept; and also the king and all his servants wept [with] a weeping great very.

en.L: And it happened, as he finished speaking, that look, the sons of the king came, and they lifted up their voice and wept. And the king also and all his servants wept [with] a very great weeping.
en.B: He had hardly finished speaking when the king's sons came in, weeping aloud. The king and all his officials also wept very bitterly.
en.R: He had just finished speaking when the king's sons arrived. They were crying loudly. The king and all his officials cried bitterly too.

es.L: Y sucedió que, al terminar él de hablar, he aquí, los hijos del rey llegaron, y alzaron su voz y lloraron. Y también el rey y todos sus siervos lloraron [con] un llanto muy grande.
es.B: Apenas había terminado de hablar cuando llegaron los hijos del rey, llorando a gritos. También el rey y todos sus oficiales lloraron con mucha amargura.
es.R: Acababa de terminar de hablar cuando llegaron los hijos del rey. Lloraban a gritos. El rey y todos sus oficiales también lloraron amargamente.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme il achevait de parler, que voici, les fils du roi arrivèrent, et ils élevèrent la voix et pleurèrent ; et le roi aussi et tous ses serviteurs pleurèrent d’un très grand pleur.
fr.B: Il achevait à peine de parler que les fils du roi arrivèrent en pleurant à grands cris. Le roi et tous ses officiers pleurèrent eux aussi très amèrement.
fr.R: Il venait juste de finir de parler quand les fils du roi sont arrivés. Ils pleuraient très fort. Le roi et tous ses officiers ont aussi pleuré amèrement.

vi.L: Vừa khi người nói xong, kìa, các con trai của vua đến, cất tiếng lên khóc. Vua và tất cả các đầy tớ vua cũng khóc [với] tiếng khóc rất lớn.
vi.B: Người vừa nói xong thì các hoàng tử đến, khóc lớn tiếng. Vua và tất cả các quần thần cũng khóc lóc thảm thiết.
vi.R: Người vừa nói xong thì các con trai của vua về đến. Họ khóc lớn tiếng. Vua và tất cả các quần thần cũng khóc rất đau đớn.

decisions.choice: lifted up their voice and wept: wept aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase describes loud weeping, the open grief of mourning (Genesis 29:11; Judges 2:4).

decisions.choice: wept with a very great weeping: the grief was deep
decisions.reason: The verb is followed by its own noun and "very great", the strongest way Hebrew has to say it. Relief that the sons are alive is swallowed up in grief for Amnon.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: As in verse 31.

source.text: וְאַבְשָׁל֣וֹם בָּרַ֔ח וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אֶל־תַּלְמַ֥י בֶּן־עַמִּיה֖וּד מֶ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּר וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֥ל עַל־בְּנ֖וֹ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And he mourned over his son all the days.

en.L: And Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And he mourned for his son all the days.
en.B: Absalom fled; he went to Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. David grieved for his son day after day.
en.R: Absalom ran away to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son Amnon day after day.

es.L: Y Absalón huyó y se fue a Talmai hijo de Amiud, rey de Gesur. Y [David] lloró por su hijo todos los días.
es.B: Absalón huyó y se fue a donde Talmai hijo de Amiud, rey de Gesur. David lloraba por su hijo día tras día.
es.R: Absalón huyó a donde Talmai hijo de Amiud, el rey de Gesur. Y David lloraba día tras día por su hijo Amnón.

fr.L: Et Absalom s’enfuit et alla chez Talmaï, fils d’Ammihoud, roi de Gueshour. Et il prit le deuil pour son fils tous les jours.
fr.B: Absalom s’enfuit et se rendit chez Talmaï, fils d’Ammihoud, roi de Gueshour. David pleura son fils jour après jour.
fr.R: Absalom s’est enfui chez Talmaï, fils d’Ammihoud, le roi de Gueshour. Et David a pleuré la mort de son fils Amnon jour après jour.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm chạy trốn và đi đến Thanh-mai con trai A-mi-hút, vua xứ Ghê-su-rơ. Còn vua thì để tang con mình suốt những ngày ấy.
vi.B: Áp-sa-lôm chạy trốn đến với Thanh-mai con trai A-mi-hút, vua xứ Ghê-su-rơ. Còn Đa-vít thì ngày nào cũng khóc thương con mình.
vi.R: Áp-sa-lôm chạy trốn đến với Thanh-mai con trai A-mi-hút, vua xứ Ghê-su-rơ. Còn Đa-vít thì ngày nào cũng khóc thương Am-nôn con mình.

decisions.choice: Talmai king of Geshur: Absalom's grandfather
decisions.reason: Absalom's mother Maacah was the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur (3:3), a small Aramean kingdom east of the Sea of Galilee. Absalom fled to his mother's family, beyond David's reach.

decisions.choice: Ammihud: the name as the scribes' notes read it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters spell the name Ammihur, and the scribes' notes read it as Ammihud. The text follows the reading of the notes, as the data does.

decisions.choice: he mourned for his son: David mourned for Amnon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name the one who mourned or the son. David is the one who can mourn "his son", and in verse 39 he is comforted for Amnon, so Amnon is most likely meant. Some take the son to be Absalom, now lost to him in exile.

decisions.choice: all the days: day after day, for a long time
decisions.reason: The phrase means continually, for the time that followed.

decisions.choice: David (Balanced, Readable); Amnon (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David as the one who mourned, and Readable names the son, following the meaning decision. Literal keeps the Hebrew "he" and "his son".

decisions.choice: Talmaï, Ammihoud, Gueshour
decisions.reason: The forms already used in the French Pentateuch (Talmaï and Ammihoud in Numbers, the Gueshourites in Deuteronomy); kept for both books.

decisions.choice: [David]
decisions.reason: The English Literal says only 'he mourned'; in Spanish the subject would read as Absalom, so Literal supplies David in brackets, as Balanced and Readable name him (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: names "Thanh-mai", "A-mi-hút", "Ghê-su-rơ"
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Vietnamese forms; kept through Samuel.

source.text: וְאַבְשָׁל֥וֹם בָּרַ֖ח וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ גְּשׁ֑וּר וַיְהִי־שָׁ֖ם שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And Absalom fled and went [to] Geshur, and he was there three years.

en.L: And Absalom fled and went [to] Geshur, and he was there three years.
en.B: So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and he stayed there three years.
en.R: After Absalom ran away to Geshur, he stayed there for three years.

es.L: Y Absalón huyó y se fue [a] Gesur, y estuvo allí tres años.
es.B: Así que Absalón huyó y se fue a Gesur, y se quedó allí tres años.
es.R: Después de huir a Gesur, Absalón se quedó allí tres años.

fr.L: Et Absalom s’enfuit et alla [à] Gueshour, et il y fut trois ans.
fr.B: Absalom s’enfuit donc à Gueshour et y resta trois ans.
fr.R: Après s’être enfui à Gueshour, Absalom est resté là-bas pendant trois ans.

vi.L: Áp-sa-lôm chạy trốn và đi đến Ghê-su-rơ, và ở đó ba năm.
vi.B: Vậy Áp-sa-lôm chạy trốn đến Ghê-su-rơ và ở đó ba năm.
vi.R: Sau khi Áp-sa-lôm trốn đến Ghê-su-rơ, chàng ở đó ba năm.

decisions.choice: Absalom fled: the third time
decisions.reason: The words "Absalom fled" come for the third time (verses 34, 37). The repetition closes the story of his flight and leads to the three years of exile.

decisions.choice: After Absalom ran away to Geshur, he stayed there
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two clauses with "after" to show the order of events.

source.text: וַתְּכַל֙ דָּוִ֣ד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לָצֵ֖את אֶל־אַבְשָׁל֑וֹם כִּֽי־נִחַ֥ם עַל־אַמְנ֖וֹן כִּֽי־מֵֽת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it was finished [?] David the king to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted over Amnon, for he was dead.

en.L: And [the spirit of] King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.
en.B: And King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon's death.
en.R: In time, King David's heart longed to go to Absalom. He had come to accept that Amnon was dead.

es.L: Y [el espíritu del] rey David anhelaba salir hacia Absalón, porque se había consolado en cuanto a Amnón, ya que estaba muerto.
es.B: Y el rey David anhelaba ir a ver a Absalón, porque ya se había consolado de la muerte de Amnón.
es.R: Con el tiempo, el corazón del rey David anhelaba ir a ver a Absalón. Había llegado a aceptar que Amnón estaba muerto.

fr.L: Et [l’esprit du] roi David languit de sortir vers Absalom, car il était consolé au sujet d’Amnon, puisqu’il était mort.
fr.B: Et le roi David languissait d’aller vers Absalom, car il s’était consolé de la mort d’Amnon.
fr.R: Avec le temps, le roi David a eu très envie d’aller voir Absalom. Il avait fini par accepter la mort d’Amnon.

vi.L: [Lòng] vua Đa-vít mong mỏi được đi ra gặp Áp-sa-lôm, vì vua đã được an ủi về Am-nôn, vì nó đã chết.
vi.B: Vua Đa-vít mong mỏi được ra gặp Áp-sa-lôm, vì vua đã nguôi ngoai nỗi đau về cái chết của Am-nôn.
vi.R: Dần dần, lòng vua Đa-vít khao khát được gặp Áp-sa-lôm. Vua đã chấp nhận được việc Am-nôn đã chết.

decisions.choice: the spirit of King David: something like "spirit" has dropped out
alternatives: David the king (Hebrew as it stands)
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine, but "David the king" is masculine, so the Hebrew seems to have lost a feminine noun such as "the spirit" or "the soul". A Hebrew manuscript from Qumran and the ancient Greek translation read "the spirit of the king". The meaning stays about David's inner self.

decisions.choice: longed to go out to Absalom: David yearned for his exiled son
alternatives: King David ceased to go out against Absalom
King David's anger against Absalom was spent
decisions.reason: The verb means to come to an end, to be spent, and with "spirit" or "soul" it means to long or pine for (Psalm 84:3). The verse can also be read: "King David ceased to go out against Absalom", that is, his anger was spent and he gave up thought of pursuing him. Both readings say that, with Amnon's death behind him, David's heart turned toward Absalom; the first reading is followed. Chapter 14 shows David still not willing to bring Absalom home without being pressed.

decisions.choice: comforted: consoled, his grief eased
decisions.reason: The verb is used of grief that has run its course (Genesis 24:67; 38:12). Time had eased David's mourning for Amnon.

decisions.choice: [the spirit of]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words that the feminine verb seems to need, from the meaning decision. Balanced and Readable say "King David" and "King David's heart", which carry the same sense.

decisions.choice: In time
decisions.reason: Readable adds "In time" to show that this came after the three years of verse 38.
